=== FILE: llms.txt ===

# AEC Model Bridge

> Open-source Revit MCP server (Model Context Protocol) and native Revit add-in. AI assistants such as Claude, Codex and Cursor read and edit the BIM model open in Revit 2024 to 2027. Every model change is a plan that a person approves first (approval gate). Also reads IFC files; Rhino, Grasshopper and Speckle integrations included.

- Protocol: Model Context Protocol, stdio transport. Any MCP client that can start a local server works.
- Tools: 330 in the default setup, counted in mock mode. Revit has 112 of them.
- Safety: tools that change the model are blocked until a plan is approved. An unattended mode exists and is opt-in.
- Platform: live Revit work needs Windows and a licensed Revit. Mock mode (sample data) needs neither.
- Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later with the Revit Linking Exception, plus a commercial option.

## Use it

- [README](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/README.md): what it does, quick start, one-click install for VS Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop.
- [Install guide](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/install.md): installer, source install, MCP client config, bridge health check, mock mode.
- [Other MCP clients](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/clients.md): config for Codex, Gemini CLI, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Windsurf and Cline.
- [Compatibility](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/compatibility.md): tested clients, agent frameworks, applications and file formats (IFC, BCF).
- [Run beside Autodesk's Revit MCP server](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/run-beside-autodesk-revit-mcp.md): tool name prefixes and a two-server client configuration (UNVERIFIED).
- [Tool catalog](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/tools-generated.md): every tool with its read or write flag.
- [Prompt library](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/prompts/README.md): 53 copy-ready prompts for BIM coordinators, each mapped to tools and the approval flow.
- [Configuration reference](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/configuration-reference.md): environment variables, runtime modes, approval modes.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): log locations, connection, approval and install errors, panel Setup check.
- [Error catalogue](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/docs/error-catalogue.md): every error kind and exception class the server returns, when it happens and what to do.
- [Full text](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/blob/main/llms-full.txt): this file and the agent docs it links, in one file.

=== FILE: AGENTS.md ===

# AEC Model Bridge: agent instructions

Revit MCP server (Model Context Protocol) with a native Revit add-in. AI clients such as Claude, Codex and Cursor read and edit BIM models through plans that a person approves.

## Layout
- `packages/mcp-server-revit/`: Python MCP server (`revit_mcp_server`, Python 3.11+, `uv`). Most testable work is here.
  - `src/revit_mcp_server/security/`: approval gate (`approval.py`), proof and revert (`proof.py`), path safety (`safe_paths.py`), workspace sandbox. Build caller-supplied paths with `safe_child` or `snapshot_file`.
  - `src/revit_mcp_server/providers/`: tool providers. `modules/<id>/`: plug-in modules (`module.json` + `module.py`).
  - `tests/`: pytest, about 3,600 tests, about 3 minutes.
- `packages/revit-bridge-addin/`: C# Revit add-in (net48, net8, net10). Windows and Revit only; not buildable in Linux CI containers.
- `packages/vscode-extension/`: VS Code extension. `packages/claude-plugin/`: Claude Code plugin (listed by `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`).
- `panel/`: approval panel (plain HTML and JS in WebView2).
- `docs/`: reference docs and ADRs (`docs/adr/00NN-*.md`). `docs/examples/rule_packs/`: example QA rule packs.
- `scripts/`: PowerShell build, release and installer scripts; Python helpers (`version.py`, `count_tools.py`, `sync_counts.py`, `changelog.py`, `make_install_links.py`).

## Commands
Run from `packages/mcp-server-revit`:
```bash
uv sync --all-extras
uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider        # full suite
uv run pytest -q tests/test_<area>.py       # narrowest file first; full suite once before committing
uv run ruff check src tests                 # CI lint
uv run python scripts/generate_tool_docs.py # after adding or changing tools; CI checks docs/tools-generated.md
python ../../scripts/version.py check       # VERSION, pyproject and manifests must agree
```
`MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock` runs the server without Revit.

## Rules
- Model writes go through plans: `plan_actions`, human approval, `execute_plan`. Never add a write path that skips the gate.
- Fail closed. Refuse with a plain-language error instead of guessing.
- Do not claim live-Revit behaviour you did not observe. Mark it UNVERIFIED (see `docs/release-checklist.md`).
- Every behaviour change needs a test and one fragment file `changes/<issue-or-branch>.md` (see `changes/README.md`); do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`. After adding or removing a tool run `python scripts/sync_counts.py` and `python scripts/make_llms_full.py`.
- Docs: plain, short, factual sentences. No hype words, no emoji, no personal data, no dated narrative.
- Commits reference issues (`Fixes #N`). Work on its own branch; PRs target `dev`. PRs into `dev` are squash-merged; `dev` into `main` uses a merge commit.
- Before taking an issue, read its comments and assignees. Skip issues labelled `claimed` or assigned to someone; a contributor who asks to take one gets assigned and labelled `claimed`.
- While a release PR (`dev` into `main`) is open, `dev` is frozen: merge nothing into `dev` until it lands.
- `README.md` and `docs/i18n/README.*.md` are for humans. Every other doc is written for agents and search. Tests check README structure, tool counts and links, so run the full suite after editing docs.

## Do not read whole
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (365 KB), `uv.lock`, `docs/tools-generated.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/mcp-token-budget.md`, `docs/i18n/`. Grep them or read a line range. Use `pytest -q` and `| tail` for long output.

# AI for Revit you can trust

**AI assistants read the Revit model you have open. By default, nothing in it changes until you approve a plan.**

Open-source Revit MCP server · Revit 2024 – 2027 · 330 tools · Claude, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Pre-release (1.6.2).** See [status and limits](#status-and-limits).

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/images/readme/revit-villa-panel.png" alt="Revit villa model beside the AEC Model Bridge panel." width="900">
</p>

AEC Model Bridge is an open-source Revit MCP server with a native Revit
add-in. AI assistants use it to read your open model and propose edits.

- **Reads run straight away.** Warnings, elements, parameters, sheets, views.
- **Writes wait for you.** The assistant drafts a plan with `plan_actions`. You
  review it in the Revit panel. `execute_plan` applies it only after you approve.
- **Every executed plan leaves a proof file** that can seed a revert plan, which
  you approve the same way.
- **No Revit here?** Mock mode returns sample data. [Try it in 60 seconds](#quick-start).

It is for BIM coordinators and managers who want an assistant to check model
quality and prepare parameter fixes while a person approves every change. You
do not need to write scripts.

<a id="status-and-limits"></a>
**Status and limits.** Try it on a copy of a project first: approving a plan
changes the open model.

- Verified live: bounded read-only checks in Revit 2024
  ([report](docs/revit-addin-live-validation-2026-10-14.md)).
- Not verified live: writes, rollback, recovery, and Revit 2025 to 2027. CI does
  not start Revit. See the [release checklist](docs/release-checklist.md).
- This page follows the development branch. The latest release may differ.

Setup is documented for Claude Desktop, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Cursor and
Codex ([compatibility](docs/compatibility.md)). The server also handles IFC,
Rhino, Grasshopper and Speckle ([integrations](#other-integrations)).

## Example workflows

| Workflow | Example request | Tools used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model review | "List the active document's warnings and find affected elements." | `revit_get_document_info`, `revit_get_warnings`, `revit_get_elements_by_type` |
| Parameter updates | "Find walls on Level 02 and propose a batch update of Comments." | `revit_get_elements_by_type`, `revit_get_element_parameters`, `revit_batch_set_parameters` |
| Drawing production | "Create sheets from this CSV and place the views." | `revit_batch_create_sheets_from_csv`, `revit_place_viewport_on_sheet` |
| IFC review | "Show this IFC file's storeys and report schema validation issues." | `ifc_get_spatial_structure`, `ifc_get_properties`, `ifc_validate` |

For a first run in Revit, try:

```text
Read the active model's warnings. Group them by description and show the
affected element IDs. Then suggest which issues to investigate first.
```

Then try a parameter correction, replacing the level and value for your project:

```text
Find walls on Level 02 and show their current Comments values. Propose setting
Comments to "Coordination reviewed" for the elements I choose. After I approve
the plan in Revit, apply it and read the values back to confirm the result.
```

IFC review runs without Revit.

Snapshot QA/QC and report modules need a compatible saved snapshot, and the
filename and workspace must match. Always pass `snapshot_id`: without it most
modules refuse in bridge mode and return sample data in mock mode
(`model_bloat` does not yet). For live inspection,
use the direct Revit tools above.

## Quick start

**In 60 seconds, without Revit (mock mode)**

1. Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
2. Add the server to your client with the JSON under Manual setup and set
   `"MCP_REVIT_MODE": "mock"`. The one-click buttons below use `bridge` mode,
   which needs Revit.
3. Restart the client and ask it to list the tools, then read the active
   document. Mock mode returns generated sample data, never your model.
4. For your own model, [install the Revit add-in](#install-the-revit-add-in) and
   switch the mode to `bridge`.

**One-click install**

[![Install in VS Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Install_in-VS_Code-0098FF?style=for-the-badge)](docs/install.md#vs-code)
[![Install in Cursor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Install_in-Cursor-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=aec-model-bridge&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyItLWZyb20iLCJnaXQraHR0cHM6Ly9naXRodWIuY29tL1NhbS1BRUMvYWVjLW1vZGVsLWJyaWRnZSNzdWJkaXJlY3Rvcnk9cGFja2FnZXMvbWNwLXNlcnZlci1yZXZpdCIsImFlYy1tb2RlbC1icmlkZ2UiXSwiZW52Ijp7Ik1DUF9SRVZJVF9NT0RFIjoiYnJpZGdlIn19)
[![Claude Desktop bundle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Desktop-.mcpb_bundle-D97757?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest)

The buttons need only uv. The workspace is `~/Documents/AEC Model Bridge`
unless you set your own. For Claude Desktop, open the `.mcpb` file from the
latest release. Live Revit work also needs [the add-in](#install-the-revit-add-in).

**Manual setup**

Live Revit automation needs Windows, a licensed Revit 2024 to 2027, Python 3.11
or newer, uv and the [add-in](#install-the-revit-add-in). Add this to
`claude_desktop_config.json` (Codex, Cursor and VS Code use the same values).
The two directory variables are optional and default to the workspace above.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aec-model-bridge": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--from",
        "git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit",
        "aec-model-bridge"
      ],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Set `"MCP_REVIT_MODE": "mock"` to list every tool and its schema without
touching a model. A root `Dockerfile` runs mock mode:
`docker build -t aec-model-bridge .`, then `docker run -i --rm aec-model-bridge`.

The [VS Code extension](packages/vscode-extension/README.md) shows connection
status. It is not on the Marketplace.

### Tools at a glance

| Area | Tools | What they do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revit | 112 | Read the model, edit elements, parameters, views, sheets, schedules, exports, worksharing |
| Approval | 6 | Plan, review, approve, execute and roll back changes; show the workspace policy |
| Modules | 130 | Snapshot inspection, parameter grids, QA/QC checks, recipes, reports, selections |
| Rhino and Grasshopper | 19 | Geometry, layers, materials, boolean operations |
| Speckle | 17 | Projects, models, versions, send and receive |
| Navisworks | 15 | Model tree, viewpoints, clash tests (in progress) |
| IFC | 7 | Read IFC files without Revit |
| Graph, snapshots, exports, jobs | 24 | Graph audits, snapshot diffs, SQLite export, background jobs |

330 tools are listed in the default setup (counted from the current server in
mock mode). Autodesk Data tools appear when APS credentials are configured. The
[tool reference](docs/tools-generated.md) lists every tool. Each tool carries
MCP annotations (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`,
`openWorldHint`), so clients can tell reads from writes.

### Advanced Revit automation

For anything the catalog does not cover, `revit_invoke_method`,
`revit_reflect_get` and `revit_reflect_set` work with public Revit API members,
and `revit_execute_python` runs IronPython inside Revit. They have the same
permissions as the Revit process. Use them only with clients and prompts you
trust.

## How it works

The MCP client talks to one Python hub, which routes each call to the provider
that owns the tool. Desktop providers talk to an add-in inside the app over
localhost.

<p align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/images/architecture-dark.png">
    <img src="docs/images/architecture-light.png" alt="Architecture: an MCP client calls the Python hub, which routes to the Revit, Rhino, Navisworks, IFC and Speckle providers." width="900">
  </picture>
</p>

<sub>Diagram source: [architecture.mmd](docs/diagrams/architecture.mmd). Regenerate the images with `python scripts/render_diagrams.py`. Teal boxes work today, amber dashed boxes are in progress, indigo shapes are external services.</sub>

### How approval works

- **Two modes you will use.** `look_only` lets the assistant read and refuses
  every tool that changes the model. `ask_first` (the default, also written
  `required`) lets it draft changes, but nothing runs until a person approves.
  `auto` switches the check off, for controlled pipelines only
  (`MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`).
- **Only a person approves.** Approving, rejecting and rolling back plans are
  not offered to AI clients. Approve in the Revit panel or with the
  `aec-model-bridge-approve` command.
- **Nothing applies on its own.** A change runs once, and only if it matches an
  approved action of an approved plan.

<p align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/images/approval-flow-dark.png">
    <img src="docs/images/approval-flow-light.png" alt="Approval flow: the assistant drafts a plan, a person approves it in the panel or the command line, and the hub runs only the approved actions." width="900">
  </picture>
</p>

<sub>Diagram source: [approval-flow.mmd](docs/diagrams/approval-flow.mmd).</sub>

The panel's Plans list shows each pending plan's tools, arguments and, when
captured, the before-value. Review text (reasoning, citations, assumptions,
warnings) must be opened before Approve is enabled. Malformed, unsupported or
oversized reviews block approval. If the panel cannot show a plan completely, it
disables Approve and points to `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>`, which
works for a plan in any state. See
[plan review in the panel](docs/security.md#plan-review-in-the-panel). Live
WebView2 approval still needs acceptance.

**Undo.** Parameter and model-edit actions each run in their own named
transaction, so Ctrl+Z undoes one action per press. Save, sync and scripts are
not covered. If every action of a plan is a parameter write, move or rotation and
the add-in lists `revit.execute_plan_batch`, the plan runs as one transaction
group named "AEC Model Bridge: <plan title> (<short id>)". One press undoes it,
and one failed action rolls the whole group back.

**Revert.** The assistant can draft a revert plan with `plan_revert` from the
proof of an executed plan, and you approve it like any other plan.
`rollback_plan` writes recorded before-values back in reverse order. It is for
people only and has no panel button or command yet, so do not count on it.
File output and other irreversible operations are not undone and get no second
confirmation yet (planned). No undo or revert path is verified in a live Revit
session (UNVERIFIED). `proofs/` bundles exist only for plans that were executed
or attempted. See [ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-approval-gate-lifecycle.md).

## Supported Revit versions

| Revit version | Add-in target | Build tools |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 | .NET Framework 4.8 | .NET 8 SDK and .NET Framework 4.8 developer pack |
| 2025 | .NET 8 for Windows | .NET 8 SDK |
| 2026 | .NET 8 for Windows | .NET 8 SDK |
| 2027 | .NET 10 for Windows | .NET 10 SDK |

CI compiles the add-in for all four years, but no year is verified in a live
Revit session. You also need Windows 10 or 11, Python 3.11 or later, and a
licensed Revit. Mock mode runs without Revit.

### Other integrations

| Integration | Status |
|---|---|
| Revit | Available. Native C# add-in. |
| IFC (IfcOpenShell) | Available. Reads IFC files without Revit. |
| Rhino and Grasshopper | Available. Connects to the Rhino add-in on `localhost:3004`. |
| Speckle | Available. Needs a Speckle client ID in your environment. |
| Navisworks Manage | In progress. Provider and tools are registered; the add-in is not finished. |
| Power BI | In progress. Provider and tool exist but are not registered in the hub. |
| Excel, Parquet and DuckDB | Planned. |

Product names and logos belong to their owners.

## Install the Revit add-in

**Easiest (Windows):** download `AECModelBridge-Setup-<version>.exe` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest),
run it, pick your Revit versions and restart Revit. It installs the add-in and
the bundled Python server. If you tick the box, it also sets up Claude Desktop
and VS Code after backing up your settings. Uninstall from Windows Settings. The steps below build from source.

### 1. Install the MCP server

To run the server without a clone, use `uvx` as in [Manual setup](#quick-start)
or the [install guide](docs/install.md#run-the-server-with-uvx). The short
`uvx aec-model-bridge` form needs a PyPI release, which does not exist yet. To
work on the source:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge.git
cd aec-model-bridge

py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e packages/mcp-server-revit
```

### 2. Install the Revit add-in

If Windows blocks the downloaded scripts, right-click each `.ps1` file, open
Properties, and select Unblock.

```powershell
$RevitVersion = Read-Host "Revit year (2024, 2025, 2026, or 2027)"

.\scripts\package.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion
.\scripts\install.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion
```

The installer places version-specific binaries in:

```text
C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\bin\<year>
```

The add-in manifest is installed per user in:

```text
%APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>
```

Add `-AllUsers` to `install.ps1` to use
`C:\ProgramData\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>` instead. To prepare every
supported version:

```powershell
.\scripts\package.ps1 -RevitVersion All
```

Each [release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest)
has a package per Revit year, for example `aec-model-bridge-revit-2026-<version>.zip`.
Unzip it and run `.\install.ps1 -RevitVersion 2026` instead of building.
`scripts/build-installer.ps1` builds an Inno Setup installer. Troubleshooting is
in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

## Connect Claude Desktop to Revit

Add the server to the `mcpServers` section of `claude_desktop_config.json`.
Codex, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients use the same `command`, `args` and
`env` values in their own format. Use the Python from your virtual environment
and a workspace folder the server may access:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aec-model-bridge": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\aec-model-bridge\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "revit_mcp_server.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    },
    "aec-model-bridge-revit-2026": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\aec-model-bridge\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "revit_mcp_server.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION": "2026",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION` to target the newest open Revit. Set it to a
year such as `2024` or `2026` to lock an entry to that version.
`MCP_REVIT_BRIDGE_URL` overrides the endpoint.

Other starting points: [`.vscode/mcp.json`](.vscode/mcp.json) and
[`docs/examples/hermes-desktop.json`](docs/examples/hermes-desktop.json) (replace
the placeholder Python path). MCP Bundle clients can use the `.mcpb` file from
the [latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest).
The add-in is still required.

### Check the connection

Restart Revit, open a model, and run:

```powershell
$registry = Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AECModelBridge\registry\revit-*.json" | Select-Object -First 1
$switch = Get-Content $registry.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
Invoke-RestMethod "$($switch.endpoint)/health"
```

The response should report `healthy` and the Revit version. In Revit, look for
the `AEC Bridge` ribbon tab. Model Bridge has Panel, Approve and Check model.
Connection has one Connected/Disconnected toggle; its slide-out has Status,
Config, Reports, Help and About.

## Security

- The Revit bridge listens on localhost only.
- The server reads and writes only inside `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`.
- Mutating tools need an approved plan unless you turn approval off.
- Approval records the channel (panel or command line) and your operating-system
  account. It does not prove who is typing, so do not give an AI client a shell
  on the account you approve with.
- Tool calls go to an audit log, and secrets are redacted.

Details: [docs/security.md](docs/security.md). To report a vulnerability, follow
[SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).

## FAQ

### What is an MCP server for Revit?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants
call tools in other software. This server publishes Revit operations as tools,
and the add-in runs them in Revit.

### Which AI assistants work with it?

Any MCP client that can start a local stdio server. Setup is documented for
Claude Desktop, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Codex. Windsurf, Cline,
Roo Code, Continue, Zed, Claude Code and Gemini CLI should work but are
untested ([compatibility](docs/compatibility.md)). The panel chat can also use
an Anthropic API key, or the `claude` or `codex` command-line tools
([ADR 0012](docs/adr/0012-native-agent-chat-backend.md)).

### Can the AI change my model without asking?

Not in the default mode. Tools that change the model are blocked until a person
approves a plan. With `MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`, approval is skipped. See
[How approval works](#how-approval-works).

### Does it send my model to the cloud?

The server, add-in and bridge run on your machine. Tool results go to the model
provider behind your client. Cloud providers such as Speckle run only when you
configure them.

### Does it work with IFC files without Revit?

Yes. The IFC provider uses IfcOpenShell to read structure, properties and
bounding boxes, query by class, GUID, name or property, and validate the schema.
It does not edit IFC files.

### Can I use it without Revit installed?

Only in mock mode. Live work needs Revit 2024 to 2027 and the add-in.

## Releases and versions

Semantic Versioning. Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`, and a root `VERSION` file
holds the version. See [docs/versioning.md](docs/versioning.md) and
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

```powershell
# Python tests

# Build all supported versions
.\scripts\package.ps1 -RevitVersion All
```

CI builds the server and the add-in for Revit 2024 through 2027. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

# Install AEC Model Bridge

AEC Model Bridge has two parts:

1. A Python MCP server that your AI client starts.
2. A native add-in that Revit loads.

You need both to work with a live Revit model. Mock mode needs only the Python
server. It uses sample data. Supported Revit versions are 2024 to 2027. For
release numbering, see [versioning](versioning.md).

## Requirements

| Revit version | Add-in target | Build requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 | .NET Framework 4.8 | .NET 8 SDK and .NET Framework 4.8 developer pack |
| 2025 | .NET 8 for Windows | .NET 8 SDK |
| 2026 | .NET 8 for Windows | .NET 8 SDK |
| 2027 | .NET 10 for Windows | .NET 10 SDK |

General requirements:

- Windows 10 or 11
- Python 3.11 or later
- Git
- A licensed Revit installation for live bridge mode

## Download the installer

This is the easiest way to install on Windows. You do not need Python, Git or build tools.

1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest)
   and download `AECModelBridge-Setup-<version>.exe`.
2. Close Revit, then double-click the file. Windows SmartScreen may warn that the
   publisher is unknown, because the installer is not code-signed yet. Choose
   **More info**, then **Run anyway**. To check the download, compare it with the
   checksum in `SHA256SUMS.txt` on the same page.
3. On the *Revit versions* page, the installer has already ticked the Revit years it
   found on your computer. Change them if you like. You can also tick *Set up Claude
   Desktop and VS Code*. The installer first copies your current settings to a
   `.aec-backup-<date>` file.
4. Start Revit and look for the **AEC Bridge** tab.

The installer needs no administrator rights. It puts the add-in in
`C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\bin\<year>`, the bundled Python and MCP server in
`C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\python`, and a per-user manifest in
`%APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>`. Running the installer again upgrades the
existing install.
To remove everything, open *Apps > Installed apps > AEC Model Bridge > Uninstall*.
Close Revit first. Both Setup and the uninstaller stop if Revit is running.

For a silent install (IT deployment):

```powershell
.\AECModelBridge-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /COMPONENTS="y2025,y2026"
```

`/COMPONENTS` takes `y2024`, `y2025`, `y2026` and `y2027`. Leave it out to use the
Revit versions the installer detects. Add `/TASKS="mcpclients"` to set up Claude Desktop
and VS Code. Add `/LOG="setup.log"` to keep a log. To build the installer yourself, see
[build and install scripts](build-and-install-scripts.md).

## Install From Source

Clone the repository and create a virtual environment:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge.git
cd aec-model-bridge

py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e packages/mcp-server-revit
```

Enter the Revit year installed on your machine:

```powershell
$RevitVersion = Read-Host "Revit year (2024, 2025, 2026, or 2027)"
```

Build, package and install the add-in for that year. To only build, run
`.\scripts\build-addin.ps1 -RevitVersion 2026` (use your Revit year):

```powershell
.\scripts\package.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion
.\scripts\install.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion
```

The default install is per user. It uses these locations:

```text
Add-in manifest:
%APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\AECModelBridge.addin

Version-specific binaries:
C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\bin\<year>\

Configuration:
C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\config\default.json
```

To install the manifest for all users:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion -AllUsers
```

To package every supported Revit version:

```powershell
.\scripts\package.ps1 -RevitVersion All
```

Then run `install.ps1` once for each Revit year you have installed.

## Install From a Release

Download a package matching your Revit version from
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases).

Extract the archive and list the folders under `bin`. Then install your year:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem .\bin -Directory
$RevitVersion = Read-Host "Choose one of the listed Revit years"
.\install.ps1 -RevitVersion $RevitVersion
```

If there is no prebuilt package for your year, use the source install above.

Check that the download was built by this repository's release workflow (needs the GitHub CLI):

```bash
gh attestation verify aec-model-bridge-revit-2026-1.6.0.zip --repo Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge
```

Use the name of the file you downloaded. The same check works for the installer, the `.mcpb` bundle and the PyPI wheel and sdist. See [Supply chain](supply-chain.md).

## Run the server with uvx

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) can fetch and start
the MCP server from this repository without a clone. This works today, without a
PyPI release:

```bash
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit" aec-model-bridge
```

The server speaks MCP over stdin and stdout, so you normally put this command in
your client configuration instead of running it in a terminal (see
[one-click install links](#one-click-install-links)). Set `MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock`
to try it without Revit. Live use still needs the Revit add-in, from the installer
or the source install above.

After the first PyPI release, the short form will be:

```bash
uvx aec-model-bridge
```

The package is not on PyPI yet, so the short form does not work today.

## Configure an MCP client

If you do not set a workspace, the server uses `~/Documents/AEC Model Bridge`.
The examples below set one explicitly. In bridge mode the server connects to the
newest open Revit by default. Set `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION` to pick a specific
Revit year:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aec-model-bridge": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\aec-model-bridge\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "revit_mcp_server.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    },
    "aec-model-bridge-revit-2026": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\aec-model-bridge\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "revit_mcp_server.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION": "2026",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES` accepts several paths separated by semicolons.

In VS Code, you can start from [`.vscode/mcp.json`](../.vscode/mcp.json).

If your client supports MCP Bundles, install the `.mcpb` file from the latest
release. You still need to install the Revit add-in separately.

## One-click install links

Each link adds the same server entry (`uvx`, mode `bridge`). No directory variables are needed. The workspace defaults to `~/Documents/AEC Model Bridge`. They need `uv` only.

```json
{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}
```

Regenerate or check the links with `python scripts/make_install_links.py` (`--json`, `--check`). `tests/test_install_links.py` decodes each link and compares it with the entry above.

### VS Code

Format: `vscode:mcp/install?` followed by `encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({name, ...server}))`. Insiders uses `vscode-insiders:mcp/install?`.

```text
vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22aec-model-bridge%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22uvx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22--from%22%2C%22git%2Bhttps%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FSam-AEC%2Faec-model-bridge%23subdirectory%3Dpackages%2Fmcp-server-revit%22%2C%22aec-model-bridge%22%5D%2C%22env%22%3A%7B%22MCP_REVIT_MODE%22%3A%22bridge%22%7D%7D
```

Command line (bash or cmd quoting):

```text
code --add-mcp "{\"name\":\"aec-model-bridge\",\"command\":\"uvx\",\"args\":[\"--from\",\"git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit\",\"aec-model-bridge\"],\"env\":{\"MCP_REVIT_MODE\":\"bridge\"}}"
```

GitHub strips `vscode:` and `cursor:` hrefs from Markdown, so the README badge links here. The `vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install` form is undocumented and returned HTTP 403 for values containing `#subdirectory=` when tested. A PyPI release would allow a plain `uvx aec-model-bridge` entry.

### Cursor

```text
cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=aec-model-bridge&config=<base64 of the server entry above>
```

The README badge uses `https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=aec-model-bridge&config=<same base64>` because GitHub strips `cursor:` links. That https form is UNVERIFIED: it is not in the Cursor docs.

### Claude Desktop

The release workflow attaches a `.mcpb` bundle. Download it from the [latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest) and open it.

## First check after install

Open a project in Revit and open the panel from the AEC Bridge tab. The Setup check card runs on load. `Ready` means all checks passed. Otherwise each failing check shows what to do; fix it and press Refresh. See [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#panel-setup-check) for each check.

Without Revit, mock mode (below) returns a small sample model: two levels, one wall, one door, two rooms. Write tools return `mock-response` and change nothing. A first prompt that works: "Which AEC Model Bridge tools do you have?". Then `model_inspector_summarize_model`, then `qaqc_checker_run_check` with the `core` pack. To try the gate in mock mode, draft a change with `plan_actions`, then approve it yourself with `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` and `aec-model-bridge-approve approve <plan_id>` in a terminal that uses the same workspace as the client. The assistant cannot call `approve_plan` or `reject_plan`.

## Update and uninstall

Close Revit before running a newer installer or uninstalling. Remove the MCP client entry yourself. The workspace holds project data and is kept. After install the server and add-in run offline; AI providers and optional cloud tools (Speckle, Autodesk) need network access.

## Verify the bridge

When Revit starts, the add-in writes an endpoint file under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\registry`. This command reads that file and calls the bridge:

```powershell
$registry = Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AECModelBridge\registry\revit-*.json" | Select-Object -First 1
$switch = Get-Content $registry.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
Invoke-RestMethod "$($switch.endpoint)/health"
```

The response should include:

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "revit_version": "<running Revit year>"
}
```

The reported year matches the Revit version that is running.

## Supported start command

The supported way to start the server is `python.exe -m revit_mcp_server` (the bundled one is `C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\python\python.exe`). `-m revit_mcp_server.mcp_server` is the same server and also works. The installer's client setup writes `python.exe -m revit_mcp_server.mcp_server`.

The bundle also has relocatable launchers `python\Scripts\aec-model-bridge.cmd`, `revit-mcp-server.cmd`, `aec-model-bridge-panel-server.cmd` and `aec-model-bridge-approve.cmd`. They call `python.exe` next to them, so they keep working if the folder moves. Releases before the fix for issue #159 shipped pip `.exe` launchers in that folder; those exit silently on a user PC. Do not point a client at an `.exe` in `python\Scripts`.

## Mock mode

Mock mode runs the MCP server without Revit. It returns sample data:

```powershell
$env:MCP_REVIT_MODE = "mock"
$env:MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR = "C:\revit-workspace"
$env:MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES = "C:\revit-workspace"

python -m revit_mcp_server
```

To run the automated tests:

```powershell
python -m pytest packages/mcp-server-revit/tests
```

## Troubleshooting

### Bridge connection refused

- Confirm Revit is running.
- Confirm the `AEC Bridge` ribbon tab is present. It has Connection, Workflows and Tools panels.
- Check that the manifest year matches the running Revit year.
- Check the bridge log at `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\bridge.jsonl`.
- Only if you turned on legacy mode (`MCP_REVIT_LEGACY_PORT=1`): confirm no other program is using port `3000`. The default mode picks a free port by itself.

### Add-in build fails

- Run `dotnet --list-sdks` and confirm the required SDK is installed.
- For Revit 2024, install the .NET Framework 4.8 developer pack.
- Confirm the selected `-RevitVersion` is one of `2024`, `2025`, `2026`, or
  `2027`.
- If Revit is not installed on the build machine, the build uses the matching
  Revit API reference packages.

### Workspace access denied

- Use absolute paths for `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR`.
- List every folder you need in `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`.
- Separate several Windows paths with semicolons.

For more settings, see the [configuration reference](configuration-reference.md)
and the [security guide](security.md).

# Other MCP clients

Status: UNVERIFIED. Snippets come from each client's documentation and were not tested on a live install. If one does not match, check the client's docs.

Before you start, finish the [install guide](install.md) (the Revit add-in is a separate install) and install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) so `uvx` is on your PATH. Each entry starts the server in live mode; set `MCP_REVIT_MODE` to `mock` to try it with sample data and no Revit. Menu names change between versions.

After saving, ask the assistant to list the AEC Model Bridge tools. With Revit open and the **AEC Bridge** tab visible, ask it to read the model name. Model changes stay blocked until you approve a plan in the Revit panel, whatever auto-approve the client has. See [privacy](privacy.md) and [security](security.md).

## Prompts and resources

Besides tools, the server offers MCP prompts and read-only resources. Support depends on the client: many show prompts as slash commands or a prompt picker, and some ignore resources.

Prompts (each is short text that names real tools; none approves anything for you):

| Prompt | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_review` | Warnings, QA/QC checks and a report. Read-only. Optional `rule_pack`, `category`. |
| `parameter_fix` | Find elements, draft a plan, wait for your approval in the panel, read back. Needs `category`, `parameter`, `value`; optional `level`. |
| `sheet_prep` | Sheet and view checks before issue. Read-only. |
| `handover_report` | Build the QA hand-over report. |
| `first_run` | A short tour that changes nothing; fine in mock mode. |

Resources (JSON, redacted like tool results, ids validated, nothing writable):

| URI | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `aec://workspace/snapshots` | Saved snapshots, newest first (up to 100). |
| `aec://snapshot/{id}/summary` | Counts, source and coverage of one snapshot, not its elements. |
| `aec://plans/pending` | Pending plan ids, state and summary. |
| `aec://plan/{id}` | One plan. |
| `aec://proof/{id}` | The proof bundle of an executed plan. |
| `aec://qa/latest` | Issue counts by severity and status for the latest QA/QC run. |

Clients that support MCP Apps can show `plan_actions` and `list_pending_plans` results in the read-only view `ui://aec-model-bridge/plan-review`. It cannot approve. See [MCP Apps plan review view](mcp-apps.md).

## Cline (VS Code)

*MCP Servers, Installed, Configure MCP Servers* opens `cline_mcp_settings.json`. Leave Cline's auto-approve off for tools that change the model. When Cline installs the server for the person, it should check `uv --version`, ask whether to use `mock` (sample data) or `bridge` (open Revit, needs the add-in from [install](install.md)), keep existing servers in the file, not set `MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_MODE`, and never approve a plan itself. Explicit panel Dev mode and timed Auto also skip per-change approvals; switch them off for this workflow.

```json
{"mcpServers":{"aec-model-bridge":{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}}}
```

## OpenAI Codex (CLI and IDE)

`~/.codex/config.toml` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml`), or run `codex mcp add`. Codex may ask before running tools; that is separate from the Revit approval gate.

```toml
[mcp_servers.aec-model-bridge]
command = "uvx"
args = ["--from", "git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit", "aec-model-bridge"]
env = { MCP_REVIT_MODE = "bridge" }
```

## Gemini CLI

`~/.gemini/settings.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\settings.json`), or `.gemini/settings.json` in one project. Add it next to existing settings. `/mcp` lists connected servers. There is no `gemini-extension.json` yet, so `gemini extensions install` does not work.

```json
{"mcpServers":{"aec-model-bridge":{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}}}
```

## JetBrains IDEs (AI Assistant)

*Settings, Tools, AI Assistant, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Add*, then choose "As JSON" and paste. The IDE keeps the file itself. Junie has its own MCP settings, not checked here.

```json
{"mcpServers":{"aec-model-bridge":{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}}}
```

## Visual Studio 2022 (17.14 or later) and 2026

`.mcp.json` next to the `.sln`, or `%USERPROFILE%\.mcp.json` for all solutions. It may also read `.vscode/mcp.json`; this repository ships [one](../.vscode/mcp.json). Note the top-level `servers` key. Use Copilot Chat in agent mode and confirm the server the first time.

```json
{"servers":{"aec-model-bridge":{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}}}
```

## Windsurf

`%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\mcp_config.json` (Cascade panel, MCP servers, configure). Create it if missing, or add to the existing `mcpServers`. Refresh the MCP list after saving.

```json
{"mcpServers":{"aec-model-bridge":{"command":"uvx","args":["--from","git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit","aec-model-bridge"],"env":{"MCP_REVIT_MODE":"bridge"}}}}
```

=== FILE: docs/compatibility.md ===

# Compatibility

AEC Model Bridge is a standard MCP server. It speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio, so any AI client that can start a local MCP server can use it with the Revit model you have open.

This page separates two groups. The first is what this repository documents and sets up. The second is what should work because it is standard MCP. The maintainers have not tried anything marked "not tested".

## AI assistants and MCP clients

| Client | Status | How to connect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Desktop | Documented here | Install the `.mcpb` bundle from the [latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest), or tick the Claude Desktop option in the installer. The README shows the `claude_desktop_config.json` entry. |
| VS Code with GitHub Copilot (agent mode) | Documented here | Use the [VS Code extension](../packages/vscode-extension/README.md), the committed [`.vscode/mcp.json`](../.vscode/mcp.json), or the install link in [install.md](install.md#vs-code). |
| Cursor | Documented here | Use the Cursor install link in the README, or add the `mcpServers` entry from the README. |
| Codex | Documented here | The README states Codex uses the same values as the Claude Desktop entry. The panel chat can also call the `codex` command-line tool. |
| Hermes Desktop | Example provided | Start from [`docs/examples/hermes-desktop.json`](examples/hermes-desktop.json). |
| Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, Continue | Same configuration shape, not tested | [clients.md](clients.md) has the entry for each. |
| Claude Code, Zed, Gemini CLI, Goose, LM Studio, JetBrains AI Assistant | Standard MCP clients, not tested | They can start a stdio MCP server. Use the same command, arguments and environment variables as the README entry. Check each client's own MCP documentation for where the entry goes. |

## Agent frameworks

Any framework with an MCP stdio client can launch the server and call its tools. Examples are the Claude Agent SDK, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and LangChain or LangGraph through an MCP adapter. None of these has been tested with this server.

## What will not work directly

A client that accepts only a remote MCP server over HTTP cannot start a local stdio server. Many browser-based chat apps work this way. Remote access is not supported. For a client on the same machine, the opt-in Streamable HTTP transport (`MCP_REVIT_HTTP=1`, loopback only, bearer token required) serves the same tools and approval gate; read [Security](security.md) first. Its live behaviour with real clients is UNVERIFIED. A proxy that exposes the server beyond loopback opens your model to anything that can reach it. The server is designed for a single machine, with the Revit add-in on loopback.

Live work always needs the Revit add-in. The server talks to a running copy of Revit on Windows.

## Applications and formats

| Tool | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revit 2024 to 2027 | Available | Native C# add-in. |
| IFC | Available | Reads IFC files without Revit running. |
| Rhino and Grasshopper | Available | Connects to the Rhino add-in on `localhost:3004`. |
| Speckle | Available | Needs a Speckle client ID in your environment. |
| Navisworks Manage | In progress | The provider and tools are registered. The add-in is not finished. |
| Power BI | In progress | The tool exists but is not registered in the hub. |
| Excel and SQLite | Available as export | The report tools write `.xlsx` and `.db` files. |

## Beside Autodesk's Revit MCP server

Using both servers in one client is UNVERIFIED. [run-beside-autodesk-revit-mcp.md](run-beside-autodesk-revit-mcp.md) lists this server's tool name prefixes and a configuration with two distinct server names.

## Where the server is listed

Registry files for the official MCP Registry (`server.json`), Smithery (`smithery.yaml`, mock mode) and Glama (`glama.json`) are in the repository root. See [release-checklist.md](release-checklist.md#7-registries-and-stores) for the state of each listing.

## Try it without Revit

Set `MCP_REVIT_MODE` to `mock`. Any client above can then browse the tools and get sample answers. Live mode does not use mock data.

=== FILE: docs/run-beside-autodesk-revit-mcp.md ===

# Run beside Autodesk's Revit MCP server

Status: UNVERIFIED. The maintainers have not run AEC Model Bridge and Autodesk's Revit MCP server in one client. This page states what this repository's tool names are and how to keep the two servers apart in client configuration. Autodesk's tool names, defaults and behaviour are not documented here because they were not observed.

## What a clash is

An MCP client lists the tools of every configured server. If two servers offer a tool with the same name, the client may show one of them, rename one, or call the wrong one. How a client resolves this differs per client and is UNVERIFIED here. Check the client's own MCP documentation.

## Tool names in this server

Every tool name starts with a prefix from a fixed list, or is one of a small set of full names. The list is checked by `tests/test_tool_name_prefixes.py`, so a new tool with an unlisted name fails the test.

| Family | Prefix |
| --- | --- |
| Revit tools | `revit_` |
| Identity mapping | `aec_` |
| Other providers | `exporter_`, `graph_`, `ifc_`, `navisworks_`, `rhino_`, `snapshot_`, `speckle_`, `autodesk_data_` |
| Modules | the module id, for example `qaqc_checker_`, `parameter_manager_`, `model_inspector_` |
| Proxied tools (`MCP_PROXY_TARGETS`) | `proxy_<name>_` or `proxy_` |

Tools without a family prefix:

| Group | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Plans and approval | `plan_actions`, `plan_revert`, `execute_plan`, `list_pending_plans`, `get_proof_bundle`, `policy_show` |
| Human-only, not listed to AI clients | `approve_plan`, `reject_plan`, `rollback_plan` |
| Jobs | `job_status`, `job_cancel` |
| Discovery | `search_tools`, `context_report`, `module_list_commands` |

The full list is in [tools-generated.md](tools-generated.md).

## Configure both servers with distinct names

Give each server its own key in the client configuration. The key is the name the client shows and, in many clients, adds to the tool name. This repository uses `aec-model-bridge`. Use any other key for the second server.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aec-model-bridge": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--from",
        "git+https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge#subdirectory=packages/mcp-server-revit",
        "aec-model-bridge"
      ],
      "env": { "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge" }
    },
    "autodesk-revit-mcp": {
      "command": "<command from Autodesk's documentation>",
      "args": ["<arguments from Autodesk's documentation>"]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the `autodesk-revit-mcp` entry with the values Autodesk documents. Other clients use the same two keys in their own format; see [clients.md](clients.md).

## Reduce overlap

- Set `MCP_REVIT_TOOL_PROFILE` to `core` or `daily` to list fewer tools. See [configuration-reference.md](configuration-reference.md) and [deferred-tool-loading.md](deferred-tool-loading.md). `search_tools` finds a hidden tool by name.
- Turn off tools per server in the client if it offers that setting.
- Write changes only through this server's plan flow: `plan_actions`, human approval, `execute_plan`. Leave the other server's write tools off or on its own approval setting. Two servers editing one open model at the same time is not tested.

## Open points

- A tool-name prefix option for the unprefixed names (`plan_actions`, `execute_plan`, `job_status` and the rest) does not exist. If a live test shows a clash, add it as a code change and follow [deprecation-policy.md](deprecation-policy.md) for any rename.
- Whether the client keeps both servers connected and routes calls correctly: UNVERIFIED.

=== FILE: docs/prompts/README.md ===

# Prompt library

Copy-ready prompts for BIM coordinators, BIM managers and computational designers who use an AI client with AEC Model Bridge. Each prompt names the tools it should lead to. Reads run freely. Every model change ends in a plan that a person approves in the Revit panel or with `aec-model-bridge-approve`.

The server also ships five MCP prompts (`qa_review`, `parameter_fix`, `sheet_prep`, `handover_report`, `first_run`); see [clients](../clients.md#prompts-and-resources). This library is longer and covers more tasks. Paste a prompt into the chat; nothing here is registered with the server.

## Files

| File | Prompts | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [model-qa-and-health.md](model-qa-and-health.md) | 8 | First look, warnings, rule packs, health score, bloat, links and worksets, levels and grids, change tracking |
| [parameters-and-data.md](parameters-and-data.md) | 8 | Completeness, bulk fill, Excel round trip, duplicate Marks, shared parameters, schedules, revert, quantities |
| [sheets-and-documentation.md](sheets-and-documentation.md) | 8 | Pre-issue audit, naming, sheets from CSV, renumbering, view placement, revisions, title blocks, PDF export |
| [views-and-annotation.md](views-and-annotation.md) | 5 | View templates, crop alignment, tagging, review views, blank-view check |
| [coordination-and-clashes.md](coordination-and-clashes.md) | 5 | Category clashes, measured overlaps, Navisworks clash triage, MEP open ends, joins and openings |
| [ifc-bcf-exchange.md](ifc-bcf-exchange.md) | 5 | IFC inspection, IDS checks, IFC export check, BCF export and import |
| [handover.md](handover.md) | 4 | QA hand-over report, Excel review pack, asset data completeness, change record |
| [scripting-execute-python.md](scripting-execute-python.md) | 5 | Read-only scripts, API lookup, write scripts under a plan, debugging, pyRevit scripts |
| [dynamo.md](dynamo.md) | 5 | Porting Dynamo Python nodes, checking graph results, data for graphs, Player scripts as recipes |
| [revit-agent-preflight-and-verify.md](revit-agent-preflight-and-verify.md) | 1 | Long system prompt for agents that build in live Revit |

## How to use a prompt

1. Pick a prompt. Replace every `{placeholder}` with your value. Leave optional parts out rather than guessing.
2. Paste it into your MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and others; see [install](../install.md)).
3. Read what the assistant reports. It should name the document, the scope and the counts before it proposes anything.
4. For a change, review the plan in the Revit panel (Plans view). Approve, or reject and say what to change.
5. Ask the assistant to read the result back. A prompt is finished when the read-back matches the plan.

Set `MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock` to try any prompt with sample data and no Revit. Mock results are sample data, not your model.

## How prompts map to the approval flow

Every prompt follows the same order:

| Step | What the assistant does | Tools (examples) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspect | Confirms the document and reads what it needs. No approval needed. | `revit_get_context`, `snapshot_take`, `revit_get_parameters` |
| Propose | Drafts a plan with exact tool arguments and a short review text. | `parameter_manager_plan_set_params`, `plan_actions` |
| Approve | A person approves in the Revit panel or with `aec-model-bridge-approve`. The assistant cannot approve, and approval tools are not offered to AI clients. | none |
| Execute | Runs the approved plan once, with exactly the approved arguments. | `execute_plan` |
| Verify | Reads the result back and reports what changed and what did not. | `snapshot_diff`, `get_proof_bundle` |
| Undo (if needed) | Drafts a revert plan from the proof bundle; it is approved like any other plan. | `plan_revert` |

Rules every prompt keeps:

- A write tool called without an approved plan is refused. In mock mode the refusal is the same as in live mode.
- `dry_run` on a write tool still needs an approved plan (observed in mock mode). Use read tools to preview instead.
- `revit_execute_python` with `mode` "read" needs no approval and cannot open transactions. With `mode` "write" it needs an approved plan.
- File outputs (PDF, IFC, BCF, Excel) do not change the model, but a file export through `revit_export` still goes through a plan. Files are written inside the workspace only.
- If the panel shows Dev mode or a timed Auto window, per-change approval is off. Switch it off for these prompts.

## Placeholders

- `{level}`: a level name as it appears in Revit, for example `Level 02`.
- `{category}`: a Revit category name, for example `Doors`, `Walls`, `Mechanical Equipment`.
- `{parameter}` and `{value}`: a parameter name and the value to set.
- `{snapshot_id}`: an id returned by `snapshot_take`. Most module tools need one; pass it rather than relying on a default.
- `{file}`: a file name inside the workspace folder.

## Test status

Each prompt has a **Tested** line:

- **Mock: exercised** means the listed tool sequence was called in `MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock` and returned without an error, or a write stopped at the approval gate as expected. The prompt text itself was not run through an AI client, and mock data says nothing about a real model.
- **Untested** means the tool sequence was not called in mock mode, usually because it needs live Revit, Navisworks or an approved plan.

No prompt here has a verified live-Revit result. Treat live behaviour as UNVERIFIED (see [release checklist](../release-checklist.md)).

## Sources

The prompt set draws on these sources. Pages were found by web search; some could not be fetched from the build environment, so claims are limited to what the search summaries showed.

- MCP prompts specification (user-controlled prompts, declared arguments, argument validation): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts
- Anthropic prompting best practices (be clear and direct, examples, XML tags): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/be-clear-and-direct
- OpenAI prompt engineering best practices (instructions first, specific format, examples): https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6654000
- Autodesk Revit API forum, "CHATgpt to help with scripts" (useful for simple API tasks and refactoring): https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/revit-api-forum/chatgpt-to-help-with-scripts/m-p/11730013
- Autodesk Revit Architecture forum, "Integrating ChatGPT with Revit": https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/revit-architecture-forum/integrating-chatgpt-with-revit/m-p/12415371
- Autodesk University, "Conversational BIM: From Prompts to Projects" (2025): https://www.autodesk.com/autodesk-university/class/Conversational-BIM-From-Prompts-to-Projects-2025
- Autodesk University, "AI-Ready BIM Foundation: Push-Button Cross-Discipline Automation with Revit MCP, Dynamo and pyRevit" (2026): https://www.autodesk.com/autodesk-university/class/AI-Ready-BIM-Foundation-Push-Button-Cross-Discipline-Automation-with-Revit-MCP-Dynamo-and-pyRevit-2026
- Autodesk University, "Design Requirements Verification with BIM Automation and AI Agents" (2026): https://www.autodesk.com/autodesk-university/class/Design-Requirements-Verification-with-BIM-Automation-and-AI-Agents-2026
- Autodesk Validation Tool documentation (model checks against project standards): https://help.autodesk.com/view/VTDOCS/ENU/
- Archgyan, "ChatGPT prompts for architects" (BIM coordination prompts; specific, contextual prompts work better): https://archgyan.com/chatgpt-prompts-for-architects
- Imaginit, "Chat GPT for Revit use" (scripts generated for Dynamo): https://resources.imaginit.com/building-solutions-blog/chat-gpt-for-revit-use
- Dynamo Python Primer (UnwrapElement, transactions): https://dynamopythonprimer.gitbook.io/dynamo-python-primer/4-revit-specific-topics/working-with-transactions
- Dynamo Primer, graph strategies: https://primer2.dynamobim.org/9_best_practices/1-graph-strategies

The Dynamo forum (forum.dynamobim.com) was searched but no thread was returned by the search tool, so no forum thread is cited.

## Contribute a prompt

1. Add it to the themed file it fits, with the next free id (for example `QA-09`).
2. Use the same fields: When to use, Prompt, Tools, Expected result, Safety (for anything that writes), Tested.
3. Name real tools only. Check names with `search_tools` or [the tool catalog](../tools-generated.md). Write tool names on the **Tools** line in backticks.
4. A prompt that changes the model must say that the assistant drafts a plan, that it cannot approve, and that it waits for the person. Never tell the assistant to approve a plan, and never name a human-only tool such as the approve, reject or rollback tools.
5. Mark it **Untested** unless you ran the tool sequence in mock mode. Do not claim live results.
6. Update the count in the table above and run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_prompt_library.py` from `packages/mcp-server-revit`. The test checks every tool name against the registry.

=== FILE: docs/configuration-reference.md ===

# Configuration reference

This page lists the environment variables, package files and runtime modes of the Revit MCP server.

## Runtime modes

The server has three modes. Set the mode with `MCP_REVIT_MODE`.

- `mock`: uses built-in sample data. Use it for tests, development and trying the tools without Revit. This is the default.
- `bridge`: connects to a running Revit add-in. The server finds the add-in through its local registry entry, or through an explicit bridge URL.
- `replay`: serves Revit responses from a recorded cassette (`MCP_REVIT_CASSETTE`) and never contacts Revit. See [Record and replay](record-replay.md).

## Environment variables

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `MCP_REVIT_MODE` | No | `mock` | Selects `mock`, `bridge` or `replay`. Set `bridge` for live Revit. |
| `MCP_REVIT_RECORD` | No | unset | Bridge mode only. Records each bridge request and response to `<workspace>/cassettes/<name>.jsonl` with secrets, paths and user names masked. A plain name (letters, digits, `_`, `-`); `1`, `true`, `on` or `yes` pick a timestamped name. A path is refused and every Revit call then reports why. A cassette can still hold model data; review it before sharing. See [Record and replay](record-replay.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_CASSETTE` | With `replay` | unset | Cassette file that `MCP_REVIT_MODE=replay` serves. A request with no recorded match fails with a plain error. |
| `MCP_REVIT_BRIDGE_URL` | No | auto-discovered | Explicit URL of the Revit bridge. Overrides registry discovery. |
| `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION` | No | newest live Revit | Revit year to pick from the local registry, such as `2024` or `2026`. |
| `MCP_REVIT_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT` | No | `http` | `http` or `pipe`. With `pipe` the server sends requests over the named pipe that the selected Revit publishes as `pipe_name` in its registry entry. If the entry has no pipe, it logs a warning and uses HTTP. Off Windows, `pipe` is refused. Unset: the value of `AEC_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT`, then `http`. Any other value makes the bridge unavailable. UNVERIFIED in live Revit. See [ADR 0021](adr/0021-named-pipe-transport.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES` | No | the workspace directory | Directories the server may read and write, separated by semicolons. The path guard checks against exactly this list. A value you set always wins. |
| `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR` | No | `~/Documents/AEC Model Bridge` | Root folder for generated files and workspace-backed tools. The server creates the default folder the first time it needs it, so a one-click install works with no configuration. |
| `MCP_REVIT_AUDIT_LOG` | No | `audit.log` | Path of the audit log. A relative path resolves against the working directory of the server process. See [Logging and audit](logging-and-audit.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_LOG_LEVEL` | No | `INFO` | Log level of the server. |
| `MCP_REVIT_REDACT_RESPONSES` | No | `off` | Masks personal data in tool responses and tool errors. `off` changes nothing extra. `basic` masks email addresses and the local OS user name. `strict` also masks person fields such as `author`, `owner`, `created_by` and `user`. Any other value fails closed to `strict`. Paths and secrets are always masked, at every level. Read on each call. It does not change what Revit or the audit log hold. |
| `MCP_REVIT_READ_MAX_CHARS` | No | `20000` | Size cap in characters for read-only tool results; `0` turns it off. Longer results are cut at list rows and carry a cursor. `response_options.max_chars` overrides it per call. A value that is not an integer is ignored. Read on each call. See [Read result cursors](read-cursors.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_READ_CURSOR_TTL` | No | `600` | Seconds a read cursor stays valid, from 1 to 3600. Read when a cursor is stored or checked. |
| `MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_MODE` | No | `ask_first` | One of `look_only`, `ask_first` (alias `required`) or `auto`; trimmed and case-insensitive. `look_only` refuses every tool that changes the model and lets reads through. `ask_first` needs a `plan_id` for an approved plan before a model change runs. `auto` turns the approval check off. Any other value fails closed to `ask_first` and logs a warning. The mode cannot be changed over MCP. Live-Revit behaviour is UNVERIFIED. See [Security](security.md). Leave it at `ask_first` unless you have a reason. |
| `MCP_REVIT_TOOL_PROFILE` | No | `full` | Which tools the MCP server lists: `full` (all, about 80k tokens), `daily` (hides Rhino, Speckle, Navisworks, IFC, MEP and a few more, about 62k), `core` (54 tools for the coordinator loop, about 14k), `learned` (`core`, the always-loaded tools and your most used tools from the local usage counts; falls back to `daily` with too little data, see [Learned profile](learned-profile.md)) or `custom` (needs the file below). Tools outside the profile are not listed and calls to them are refused. Read once at startup; restart the MCP server to change it. Approval tools are always visible. See [MCP token budget](mcp-token-budget.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_TOOL_PROFILE_FILE` | No | unset | JSON file with `include` / `exclude` provider or module ID globs. Required for `custom`; narrows `full`, `daily`, `core` or `learned`. |
| `MCP_REVIT_LEARNED_TOP_N` | No | `25` | How many of the most used tools of the last 30 days `learned` adds to `core` and the always-loaded tools. Whole number from 1 to 200; any other value stops the server at startup. |
| `MCP_REVIT_USAGE_COUNTS` | No | `off` | `on` turns on local tool usage counts in `<workspace>/usage/tool-usage.json`: tool names, calls per day and last-used day only. `off` (or `0`, `false`, `no`) counts nothing and writes no file; `learned` then falls back to `daily`. Any other value stops the server at startup. Nothing is sent anywhere. See [Learned profile](learned-profile.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_HTTP` | No | `0` | `1` serves MCP over Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` instead of stdio. Off by default: no port is opened. Any value other than `1`/`0` (also `true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) stops the server at startup. See [Security](security.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_HTTP_TOKEN` | Yes, when `MCP_REVIT_HTTP` is on | none | Bearer token for the HTTP transport, at least 16 characters. Clients send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server refuses to start without it and never logs it. |
| `MCP_REVIT_HTTP_HOST` | No | `127.0.0.1` | Only `127.0.0.1` or `localhost` is accepted (both bind 127.0.0.1). Any other value stops the server at startup. |
| `MCP_REVIT_HTTP_PORT` | No | `8765` | Port of the HTTP transport, 1 to 65535. |
| `MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_TTL` | No | `28800` (8 hours) | Seconds an approved plan stays usable. After that the plan moves to `expired` and a person must approve a new plan; it is never renewed silently. `0` turns the limit off. A negative, fractional or non-numeric value falls back to the default (it never turns the limit off) and logs a warning. Checked when a call runs, not by a timer. See [ADR 0017](adr/0017-approval-document-binding-and-expiry.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_PENDING_TTL` | No | `1209600` (14 days) | Seconds a drafted, not yet approved plan can still be approved. Older pending plans are left out of `list` and `list_pending_plans` (counted as `expired_hidden`; `list --all` or `include_expired` shows them), cannot be approved, and are never deleted. `0` turns the limit off. Same fallback rule as above. |
| `MCP_REVIT_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | No | `300` | Seconds a direct MCP tool call may run. `0` turns the default off. A negative or non-numeric value falls back to `300` and logs a warning. Not applied to `run_async` jobs, MCP tasks or panel hub calls. A read that runs out of time is stopped and refused with kind `tool_timeout`. A write is not stopped and not reported as failed, because it may still be running in Revit: its approved action stays used and is recorded as running (`timeout_<id>`), like a call that came back `running`, so it is never run again. If the write finishes while the server runs, the action is closed with its real result; otherwise a person runs `aec-model-bridge-approve recover`. Read once at startup. See [Timeouts and rate limits](#timeouts-and-rate-limits). |
| `MCP_REVIT_TOOL_TIMEOUTS` | No | unset | JSON object of per-tool timeouts in seconds, for example `{"revit_export_ifc": 1800}`. `0` means no timeout for that tool. An invalid entry is ignored with a warning. Read once at startup. |
| `MCP_REVIT_RATE_LIMITS` | No | see [Timeouts and rate limits](#timeouts-and-rate-limits) | `off`, or a JSON object that changes the token buckets. A refused call did not run and did not use an approved action; it returns kind `rate_limited` with `retry_after_seconds`. An invalid value keeps the defaults and logs a warning; it never turns a limit off. Read once at startup by the MCP server and by the panel hub. |
| `MCP_REVIT_POLICY_FILE` | No | unset | Path of a policy file (YAML or JSON) that adds refusals to `plan_actions` and `execute_plan`. Unset: `policy.yaml`, `policy.yml` or `policy.json` in the workspace folder, if present. A file that is named but missing or invalid refuses every write. See [Policy file](#policy-file). |
| `MCP_REVIT_MACHINE_POLICY_FILE` | No | unset | Path of the machine policy file: the policy keys plus `allowed_tiers` and `blocked_tiers` (`read`, `write`, `script`, `export`). Unset: `%PROGRAMDATA%\AECModelBridge\policy.yaml` on Windows (UNVERIFIED) or `/etc/aec-model-bridge/policy.yaml`. A named file that is missing refuses every write. Merged with the workspace policy; the stricter rule wins. See [Security](security.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_MCP_APPS` | No | `auto` | Read-only plan review view `ui://aec-model-bridge/plan-review` (MCP Apps) and the `_meta.ui` keys on tools. The view cannot approve. `auto`: `_meta.ui` only for clients that declare the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension. `always`: for every client. `off`: no view and no `_meta.ui`. `true` and `false` mean `auto` and `off`. Read at startup. See [MCP Apps plan review view](mcp-apps.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_LOCALE` | No | `en` | Language of tool descriptions, as a two-letter code such as `nl`. Only description text changes; tool names, titles, schemas and safety annotations stay the same. A tool with no text in the catalog keeps its English description. An unknown code logs a warning and uses English. Catalogs are `locales/<code>.json` in the server package; `nl` is a small sample of 7 read-only tools, not a full translation. Read at startup. |
| `MCP_REVIT_VALIDATE_BRIDGE_PAYLOADS` | No | on | Checks each Revit add-in command payload against `contracts/bridge-commands.json` before sending. A payload that does not fit is refused and nothing is sent. `0`, `false`, `off` or `no` turns the check off; any other value keeps it on. Read on each call. See [Add-in command contract](bridge-command-contract.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_ENABLE_USER_MODULES` | No | `false` | Set to `true` to load modules from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\modules`. See [Module authoring](module-authoring.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_ALLOW_PYTHON_HOST` | No | `false` | Set to `true` to allow tools that run raw Python on the host, such as `revit_execute_python`. Leave it off unless you need it. |
| `MCP_REVIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | No | unset | Anthropic API key for the panel's built-in Claude chat (`agent_native.py`, ADR 0012). If you do not set it, the Claude chat falls back to the `claude` command-line tool when that is on your PATH. If neither is available, no AI provider is available. You can also put the key in a `.env` file. The hub reads it only at startup, so restart Revit after you set or change it. The panel's Settings view cannot set it. |
| `MCP_PANEL_HTTP_PORT` | No | `8787` | Port of the panel hub (loopback only). Read by the hub and by the add-in. |
| `AEC_PANEL_MAX_THREADS` | No | `32` | Most request threads the panel hub runs at once, `4`-`256`. Two are kept for requests whose path is `/execute` (all tools on that route, since the tool name is in the body). When every slot is in use, a new connection gets HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 1` and `{"ok": false, "kind": "hub_busy", "error": ...}`, and no thread starts. A non-numeric or out-of-range value falls back to `32` and logs a warning. Read once when the hub starts. See [Timeouts and rate limits](#timeouts-and-rate-limits). |
| `MCP_PANEL_TOKEN_FILE` | No | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\panel-hub.token` | Path of the per-user panel hub token file. The first hub to start creates it (owner-only); the hub and every Revit add-in read it. Delete it and restart the hub to rotate the token. Never copy its contents into a config, chat or log. See [Security](security.md). |
| `MCP_PANEL_REVIEWER_TOKEN_FILE` | No | `panel-reviewer.token` beside the panel token file | Path of the optional read-only reviewer token file. Off when the file is absent. Create it with `python -m revit_mcp_server.security.panel_token --new-reviewer`. A client sends it as header `X-AMB-Reviewer-Token`; it may list plans and read proofs and is refused (403) on approve, reject and approval-mode changes. See [Security](security.md). |
| `AEC_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT` | No | unset | Read by the Revit add-in at start-up. Set to `pipe` to open a named pipe for the current Windows user beside the HTTP port, and publish its name in the registry entry. The Python server also reads it when `MCP_REVIT_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT` is unset. UNVERIFIED in live Revit. See [ADR 0021](adr/0021-named-pipe-transport.md). |
| `MCP_REVIT_LEGACY_PORT` | No | unset | Read by the Revit add-in, not the Python server. Set to `true` or `1` to bind the add-in to fixed port `3000` with no authentication. See [Security](security.md). |
| `AEC_BRIDGE_TURN_BUDGET_MS` | No | `40` | Read by the Revit add-in when Revit starts. Milliseconds one Revit turn may spend on queued read-only requests before it hands control back to Revit. Clamped to `0`-`200`; `0` runs one request per turn. Writes, unknown commands, exports, `revit.extract_snapshot` and `revit.check_clashes` always run alone in their own turn. A turn can exceed the budget by at most one command. Live behaviour is UNVERIFIED. |
| `AEC_BRIDGE_FAST_WAKE` | No | unset (off) | Read by the Revit add-in when Revit starts. `1` or `true` attaches an `Idling` handler that calls `SetRaiseWithoutDelay` while requests are still queued after a turn, so the next turn starts at once. CPU cost: Revit keeps one core busy while the handler is attached. It is attached only while the queue is non-empty and removed when it is empty, so idle CPU use stays at zero. The first request after an idle period still waits for Revit's normal pickup. Live behaviour is UNVERIFIED. |
| `AEC_BRIDGE_PYTHON_RECYCLE_RUNS` | No | `50` | Read by the Revit add-in when Revit starts. Scripts one warm IronPython engine runs before it is replaced (`revit_execute_python`). Clamped to `1`-`10000`; `1` turns the warm engine off: every script starts a new engine and it is shut down when the script ends. Only read-mode scripts share it: a write-mode script always starts a new engine, which is shut down when it ends. The reset that puts back stdout, stderr and sys.path runs at the end of each read-mode script, inside its read guard, so nothing the script left behind runs outside the guard. The engine is also replaced when the active document changes, when that reset fails, after a fatal runtime error, and after a script that touched the model in read mode or left a transaction open. Each script gets a new scope and its own output. Imported modules stay loaded between scripts. Live behaviour is UNVERIFIED. |
| `REVIT_SDK` | Build only | unset | Optional path used by the add-in build scripts. |

The Revit add-in honors the same explicit directory allowlist as the hub; it
does not add its default workspace to an explicit list. When the add-in launches
the hub without an allowlist, it scopes the hub to the effective workspace,
including a custom `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR`.

## Package and registry files

These files define the Python package and the MCP registry entry:

- `packages/mcp-server-revit/pyproject.toml`
- `packages/mcp-server-revit/manifest.json`
- `server.json`

The package name is `aec-model-bridge`. The official repository is https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge.

## MCP client example

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "revit": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["-m", "revit_mcp_server.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "MCP_REVIT_MODE": "bridge",
        "MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION": "2026",
        "MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR": "C:\\RevitProjects",
        "MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES": "C:\\RevitProjects"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Timeouts and rate limits

Code: `src/revit_mcp_server/call_limits.py`. Tested with fakes and a fake clock; behaviour against a live Revit is UNVERIFIED.

Rate limits are token buckets. A bucket holds up to `burst` calls and refills at `per_minute`. A call needs one token from every bucket that applies to it, or it is refused and takes none.

| Key in `MCP_REVIT_RATE_LIMITS` | Default | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | 600 per minute, burst 300 | every MCP tool call of one client session |
| `write_tool` | 120 per minute, burst 60 | each tool that can change the model, counted per tool |
| `read_tool` | 300 per minute, burst 150 | each other tool, counted per tool |
| `tools` | none | per-tool buckets that replace `write_tool` or `read_tool` for the named tools |
| `panel_execute` | 600 per minute, burst 300 | the panel hub `/execute` route |
| `panel_chat` | 30 per minute, burst 10 | the panel hub `/agent/chat` route |

Each value is `{"per_minute": N, "burst": M}`. `per_minute` 0 turns that bucket off. Missing keys keep their defaults. Example:

```json
{"session": {"per_minute": 300, "burst": 100}, "tools": {"revit_export_ifc": {"per_minute": 2, "burst": 1}}}
```

- Approval tools (`approve_plan`, `reject_plan`, `rollback_plan`) are human-only. They are refused on MCP before any count, and the person's approve, reject and rollback calls on `/execute` are never limited.
- The MCP refusal is kind `rate_limited` with `error.retry_after_seconds`. The hub answers HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header and `{"ok": false, "kind": "rate_limited", "retry_after_seconds": N}`.
- The hub sets a 30 s socket timeout on each connection, so a stalled request body cannot hold a handler thread forever. It does not limit how long a tool call runs.
- The hub runs at most `AEC_PANEL_MAX_THREADS` request threads (default 32), two of them kept for `/execute`. Over the cap it answers HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 1` and kind `hub_busy` without starting a thread.

## Policy file

An optional policy adds refusals. It never approves or runs anything, and it can only make the server say no more often. Without a file nothing changes.
