The file is read every time it is needed, so a change applies to the next draft and to the next `execute_plan` of a plan that was drafted earlier. `policy_show` (read-only) returns the effective policy and its hash; the hash is also stored on each plan as `policy_hash`. An example is in [examples/policy.yaml](examples/policy.yaml).

| Key | Type | Refuses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blocked_tools` | list of tool names | any action that uses a listed tool |
| `allowed_tools` | list of tool names | any action whose tool is not listed (when the key is present) |
| `allowed_categories` | list of category names (`OST_` prefix and case ignored) | a plan that touches another category, or one whose category is unknown |
| `blocked_parameters` | list of parameter names (case ignored) | any action that sets a listed parameter |
| `max_elements_per_plan` | whole number | a plan naming more elements, or any action that names none |
| `max_actions_per_plan` | whole number | a plan with more actions |
| `require_second_approver` | `true` or `false` (default off) | an approval by the person who asked for the plan (two-person rule). A plan drafted while it is on records `requested_by`, covered by the plan hash. The requester is `MCP_REVIT_REQUESTER` in the server's environment, else the operating-system account; the approver is `MCP_REVIT_APPROVER` in the environment of the panel hub or `aec-model-bridge-approve`, else the account. Names are compared ignoring case and any domain part (`alice`, `alice@corp` and `CORP\alice` are the same person). An unknown requester, an unknown approver, or a plan drafted before the option was on is refused. On in either the machine or the workspace file means on. The rule is checked again at `execute_plan`: a plan with no recorded requester, or approved by its requester, does not run. **Not an authentication control:** the approver name comes from `MCP_REVIT_APPROVER` or the operating-system account and is not verified, so one person with a shell can set another name. A separate approver needs a separate operating-system account or a separately configured approving machine. |

Element, category, level and workset values come from the action arguments and, when the plan names one, the snapshot. Anything not known is reported as `unknown`; a rule that needs an unknown value refuses rather than guesses. An unknown key, a wrong type, a missing file named by `MCP_REVIT_POLICY_FILE` or a parse error is an invalid policy: every `plan_actions` and `execute_plan` call is refused with the reason until it is fixed. Direct writes in Dev or Auto mode do not go through a plan and are not covered.

## Plan preview and risk

`plan_actions`, `list_pending_plans` and `aec-model-bridge-approve show` add `preview` (rows of element id, UniqueId, parameter, before, after, tool), `preview_markdown` (the same table, at most 25 rows and an "N more" line) and `blast_radius` (`element_count`, `action_count`, `categories`, `levels`, `worksets`, `risk`). They are computed when a plan is shown, are not stored and are not part of the plan hash. Risk is `low` up to 10 elements and 5 actions, `medium` up to 100 elements and 25 actions, `high` above that. A plan is at least `medium` when an action names no element or a tool name says delete, purge or remove. These are estimates from the arguments, not a check of the live model.

## Command-line review (`aec-model-bridge-approve`)

`aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>`, `--show <plan_id>` and `approve <plan_id>` print the same review before anything else happens:

- one table per action: element (id, plus name and Mark when the plan's snapshot can be read), parameter, old value -> new value. An action that sets no parameter shows its other arguments as the new value. An old value that was not recorded shows `(not captured)`.
- counts (actions, elements, parameters, changes, old values captured), tools and the risk estimate above.
- warnings: review warnings (hashed), unhashed legacy warnings, preview notes (actions that name no element, old values not captured, high risk), expiry and malformed actions.
- the short plan hash, the approval mode in force, the expiry time (`pending_ttl` or `approval_ttl`) and the document binding. The full hash is printed at the end; the approval is bound to it.

Old values and arguments come from the hashed plan. Element names and marks come from the snapshot and are not part of the hash.

Output is plain ASCII layout with no ANSI codes, so it works in Windows cmd and PowerShell. `--color` adds color only when stdout is a terminal that supports it (on Windows: Windows Terminal, ConEmu, ANSICON, VS Code or a set `TERM`) and `NO_COLOR` is unset or empty. Long values wrap to the terminal width (60 to 200 columns) without collapsing spaces. Text values print as JSON strings in double quotes, so `"A B"`, `"A  B"` and `" "` look different. Model text is escaped. Without `--all`, at most 30 change rows and 300 characters per value are printed, followed by a `+N more ..., use --all` line. Arguments of a parameter write that are not in the Element, Parameter or New column (for example the `filter` of `revit_batch_set_parameters_by_filter`) are printed on an `Other arguments:` line under the action's table, cut by the same rule. When anything is cut, `approve` says so above the confirmation prompt.

| Option | Commands | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--show PLAN_ID` | none (top level) | Print the review and exit. Never approves. Same as `show PLAN_ID`. |
| `--all` | `--show`, `show`, `approve`, `reject`, `recover` | Print every row and full values. |
| `--json` | `--show`, `show` | Print the review as JSON and exit. Not accepted by `approve`. |
| `--color` | `--show`, `show`, `approve`, `reject`, `recover` | Color the review when supported (see above). |

The JSON review has `schema: "aec-model-bridge/plan-review"`, `schema_version: 1`, `plan_id`, `state`, `created_at`, `plan_hash`, `plan_hash_short`, `approval_mode` (`mode`, `configured_mode`, `auto_expires_at`), `expiry` (`applies`, `expired`, `reason`, `rule`, `ttl_seconds`, `expires_at`), `binding` (`recorded`, `bound`, and when bound `doc_title`, `revit_version`, `active_view_id`), `counts`, `tools`, `risk`, `warnings` (`source`, `text`), `approvable`, `not_approvable_reasons`, `actions` (each with `changes`: `element_id` as a string or null, `element_name`, `mark`, `unique_id`, `parameter`, `old`, `old_captured`, `new`, `new_is_arguments`; and `other_arguments`, the arguments no change column shows), `review`, `not_hashed_keys`, `snapshot_id` and `reverts_plan_id`. Values are not cut. `approvable` only reflects the plan's state, expiry and shape; it does not approve anything.

Approval is unchanged: the person types the plan id after the review. Without a terminal the command refuses unless `--yes` is given. The review never changes the plan file.

## Notes

- Run the server from the repository root, or from an environment where you installed the package in editable mode.
- For live Revit, install the add-in and start the Revit version you want before you test.
- To use several open Revit versions side by side, add one MCP client entry for each version. Give each entry its own `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION`.

=== FILE: docs/troubleshooting.md ===

# Troubleshooting

Find your symptom, check the likely cause, and try the fix. Every entry says where to look and what to copy into a bug report.

Each entry comes from a failure mode in the code. Claims about Windows, antivirus or a particular AI client that the code cannot show are tagged **UNVERIFIED**.

## Run the doctor

```text
aec-model-bridge doctor
python -m revit_mcp_server doctor --json
```

(`aec-model-bridge-doctor` is the same command.) Without `--fix` it reads your setup and changes nothing: Python version, package version against `VERSION`, mode, whether the workspace exists and is writable, the Revit add-in registry entry and whether it has a session token (Windows only; "N/A" elsewhere; the token value is never shown), whether the bridge port answers within one second, `ifcopenshell`, other optional packages, and the MCP client config files it knows (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Codex). A client entry that points at an `.exe` launcher under `python\Scripts` is flagged FAIL ([#159](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/issues/159)); use `uvx` or `python -m revit_mcp_server`. Exit code 0 means no FAIL, 1 means at least one. Paste the table into a bug report; it carries no tokens or client environment values.

The table is followed by the fixes the doctor could apply. `aec-model-bridge doctor --fix` applies them, prints each result, then prints the table for the state after the fixes:

- creates a missing workspace folder;
- gives the owner read, write and search access to a workspace folder the current user owns (POSIX);
- deletes add-in registry files whose Revit process is not running (Windows), and checks again just before each delete;
- points a client entry that FAILs (an `.exe` launcher or a missing command) at the Python running the doctor, as `<python> -m revit_mcp_server`. The old file is kept as `<file>.aec-backup-<timestamp>`; `env` and every other key stay as they are. Codex (`config.toml`) entries are listed for a manual edit.

It never starts or contacts Revit, never deletes user data and never changes approval settings. Unreadable registry files and config files that do not parse are left alone. The Windows fixes are UNVERIFIED on Windows.

## Error codes

A failed tool call carries an error kind (`structuredContent.error.kind`) or, for module tools, a result `kind` with a `hint`. The [error catalogue](error-catalogue.md) lists every kind and exception class, when it happens and what to do.

## Where the logs are

| Log | Location | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add-in log | `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\bridge.jsonl` | What Revit received and ran. Rolls over daily. |
| Panel hub log | `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\panel-hub.log` | The hub the Revit panel talks to. Rotates at about 1 MB and keeps 3 old files. |
| Bridge registry | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\registry\revit-<pid>.json` | The address and session token the add-in publishes when Revit starts. |
| Plans and proofs | `<workspace>\plans\` and `<workspace>\proofs\` | One JSON file per plan and per finished plan. |
| Audit log | `audit.log` in the server's working directory | Only written by the legacy server. The main server does not write it. See [logging and audit](logging-and-audit.md). |
| MCP client log | Depends on your client | Where the client shows why it could not start the server. UNVERIFIED: the location differs by client, so look in its settings or help menu. |
| Installer log | The path you give to `/LOG=` | Only when you ran the installer with that switch. See [install](install.md#download-the-installer). |

The workspace is `~/Documents/AEC Model Bridge` unless you set `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR`.

**Quick check of the whole setup:** while the panel hub runs, request its authenticated diagnostics from your own PowerShell terminal:

```powershell
$tokenFile = if ($env:MCP_PANEL_TOKEN_FILE) { $env:MCP_PANEL_TOKEN_FILE } else { Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'AECModelBridge/panel-hub.token' }
$headers = @{ 'X-AMB-Token' = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $tokenFile -Raw).Trim() }
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8787/diagnostics -Headers $headers
Remove-Variable headers
```

It returns checks including `hub`, `mode`, `revit_bridge`, `workspace` and `ai_provider`, with a `next_step` for failures. Use the port in `MCP_PANEL_HTTP_PORT` if changed. Opening the URL in an ordinary browser returns 401 because it lacks the token. Do not print or share the token or request headers.

## What to copy into a bug report

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/issues) and include:

- The exact error text, copied, not retyped.
- Your Revit year and the AEC Model Bridge version (the installer file name or `VERSION`).
- How you installed: installer, release package, source, or `uvx`.
- The mode: `mock` or `bridge`.
- The last 50 lines of `bridge.jsonl` and `panel-hub.log`.
- The output of `/diagnostics`, if the hub is running.
- The plan file from `plans\` if the problem is about a plan. Remove project names first.

Do not paste the session token from a registry file (`session_token`), the panel hub token, or any API key.

---

## Connection problems

### The bridge is not found, or there is no registry file

**You see:** an error such as `No live Revit 2026 bridge found. Available Revit versions: none.` Or the server runs and every Revit tool fails. Or the folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\registry` is empty or missing.

**Cause:** the add-in writes a registry file when Revit starts. The server reads that file to find the bridge and rejects stale sessions. No valid entry can mean the add-in did not start or Revit is not running. Server discovery does not delete registry files.

If you set `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION`, the server only accepts a bridge for that year. With no registry entry and no year set, it falls back to port 3000 and logs that tokenless connections are deprecated.

**Fix:**

1. Start Revit and open a project.
2. Check for the **AEC Bridge** tab on the ribbon. If it is missing, the add-in did not load. Check that the add-in was installed for your Revit year (see [install](install.md)).
3. Look for a `revit-<pid>.json` file in the registry folder.
4. If `MCP_REVIT_HOST_VERSION` is set, make sure it matches the running Revit year, or remove it.
5. Restart your AI client so the server reads the registry again.

**Look at:** the registry folder, `bridge.jsonl` (it logs `Wrote registry file`), and the add-in install folder `C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\bin\<year>`.

### The token does not match (401 Unauthorized)

**You see:** an error that mentions `401` or `Unauthorized` when a tool calls Revit.

**Cause:** the add-in creates a new random token each time Revit starts and writes it to the registry file. The server reads the token once, when it starts, and keeps it. If you restart Revit while your AI client stays open, the server holds the old token. The add-in rejects every request except `/health` when the token is wrong.

**Fix:** restart your AI client, or start a new chat that starts a new server, so the server reads the new registry file. Do not copy tokens by hand.

**Look at:** `bridge.jsonl`, and the time in the `started_at` field of the registry file compared with when you started Revit. **Copy to the bug report:** the error text and `started_at`. Not the token.

### Revit is not running

**You see:** `Bridge unreachable at http://127.0.0.1:... Ensure Revit is running with the AEC Model Bridge add-in loaded.` The server retries three times before it gives up, so the error can take a few seconds to appear. The client may also show `Make sure: 1. Revit is running ...`.

**Cause:** the server cannot reach the add-in. Revit is closed, still starting, or the add-in is not loaded.

**Fix:** start Revit, open a project, wait for the **AEC Bridge** tab, and try again. If Revit is open, run the health check in [install](install.md#verify-the-bridge). Check that the add-in year matches the running Revit year.

### Revit was restarted and calls say the session changed or closed

**You see:** `The selected Revit 2024 session (process N) changed or closed. Call revit_reconnect, or restart this MCP client ...`

**Cause:** the server is pinned to the Revit process it found at start. It refuses to send anything to a replacement Revit on its own.

**Fix:** call `revit_reconnect`. It lists the live Revit sessions (process id, version, start time, active document) and binds the only one, or the one named by `pid`. It repeats the health check only: it sends no model request and does not change plans, approvals, the panel token or workspace checks. Then call `revit_get_context`, and check the model before repeating an earlier write. It is refused in mock mode, with an explicit bridge URL, and inside a panel-routed call. Tested with a simulated registry; a real Revit restart is UNVERIFIED live.

### The panel hub cannot start, port 8787 is in use

**You see:** the Revit panel shows a connection error. `panel-hub.log` is empty or missing. The `bridge.jsonl` file may hold `Launched the panel hub but it never became reachable on 127.0.0.1:8787`.

**Cause:** the add-in starts a small background hub for the panel on port 8787. If something already answers `/health` on that port, the add-in leaves it alone and uses it. If another program holds the port and does not answer like the hub, the new hub cannot start. A second reason is that no Python could be found. `bridge.jsonl` then says `no Python interpreter could be found`.

**Fix:**

- Port in use: find the program using port 8787 and close it. Or set the environment variable `MCP_PANEL_HTTP_PORT` to a free port (for example `8788`) for both Revit and the hub, then restart Revit.
- No Python: install Python 3.11 or later, or set `AEC_MODEL_BRIDGE_PYTHON` to the full path of a `python.exe`. The installer ships a Python at `C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\python\python.exe`, which the add-in tries first.
- To start the hub by hand: `aec-model-bridge-panel-server` or `python -m revit_mcp_server.panel_server`.

**Look at:** `bridge.jsonl` and `panel-hub.log`.

### "No active document"

**You see:** a tool fails with `No active document`.

**Cause:** the add-in handles requests for the active Revit document. None is open. This happens at the Revit start screen, or when only a family or a non-project window is active. Tool errors come from the add-in (`BridgeCommandFactory.cs`).

**Fix:** open a project in Revit and make its window the active one. Try the tool again.

**Look at:** `bridge.jsonl` for the failing request.

---

## Panel setup check

The panel's Setup check card calls the hub's `GET /diagnostics` (127.0.0.1, port 8787 unless `MCP_PANEL_HTTP_PORT` is set) and retries every five seconds. If the card stays on "Checking setup", restart Revit and read `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\bridge.jsonl`.

| Check | If it fails |
|---|---|
| `hub` | The panel cannot reach the Python hub. Restart Revit, or run `aec-model-bridge-panel-server`, then press Refresh. |
| `mode` | The hub is in mock mode and returns sample data. Set `MCP_REVIT_MODE=bridge` and restart the hub. |
| `revit_bridge` | No running Revit has the add-in. Open Revit with the AEC Bridge tab and a project. Check the add-in year matches the Revit year. |
| `workspace` | The workspace is not writable. Set `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR` to a writable absolute path that is also in `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`. |
| `ai_provider` | Chat has no AI. Set `MCP_REVIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or sign in to the `claude` or `codex` CLI, then restart Revit. Plans and reports do not need it. |

Response shape: `{ "ok", "approval_mode", "approval_mode_note", "dev_mode", "auto_expires_at", "checks": [ { "id", "ok", "detail", "next_step" } ] }`. The `approval_mode` check fails for `auto` because `auto` skips approvals. `/health` returns a minimal status and needs no token. See [ADR 0018](adr/0018-explicit-development-mode.md).

## Approval problems

### Live mode rejects an empty snapshot_id

**You see:** `... requires a snapshot_id when connected to Revit (mode='bridge'). Capture one first with the snapshot tool and pass its snapshot_id; generated mock data is only used when MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock.`

**Cause:** the QA check, parameter manager, report generator and clash triage will not fall back to sample data in live mode. This is on purpose. Sample data must never pass for your model.

**Fix:** ask the assistant to take a snapshot (`revit_extract_snapshot`) and pass the `snapshot_id` it returns to the next tool. If you meant to try the tools without Revit, set `MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock`.

**Look at:** the tool result text. Some other modules, for example `model_inspector`, may behave differently in live mode. UNVERIFIED: check the tool's own error message.

### The approval gate blocks a tool because there is no plan_id

**You see:** `Approval Gate Blocked: Approval mode is enabled. Mutating tool '<name>' requires a valid 'plan_id' parameter.`

**Cause:** a tool that changes the model was called without a plan. The gate is on by default.

**Fix:** ask the assistant to make a plan with `plan_actions`, review and approve it yourself in the panel or human approval CLI, then run `execute_plan`. The default `ask_first` mode enforces approval; `required` is an alias. `look_only` refuses writes, and unknown values fall back to `ask_first`. `auto` and explicit panel Dev mode bypass approval checks. See [configuration](configuration-reference.md).

### The plan is not approved

**You see:** `Plan '<id>' is in state 'pending', not 'approved'. Execution blocked.` The state may also be `rejected`, `executed`, `partial` or `rolled_back`. You may also see `Plan '<id>' does not exist.`

**Cause:** the plan is waiting for approval, was rejected, or already ran. A plan id that does not exist usually has a typo, or the server is using a different workspace folder than the one that holds the plan file.

**Fix:** list pending plans. Approve the right one in the panel (Plans tab, then Approve). For a rejected or finished plan, make a new plan. If the plan file is missing, check that your client and the hub use the same `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR`.

**Look at:** `<workspace>\plans\<plan_id>.json` and its `state` field. **Copy to the bug report:** that file, with project names removed.

### Approve does nothing in the panel

**Cause:** the hub may have refused the call. The panel Run Log shows a `Plan approve` entry as soon as you click, even if the hub says no.

**Fix:** press Refresh and check the plan state. An `Error: plan.approve` entry in the Run Log means the hub rejected the call. Check `panel-hub.log`.

---

## Workspace and files

### The workspace is not writable

**You see:** in `/diagnostics`, the `workspace` check fails with `Workspace is not writable`. Or a tool says a path `is outside the allowed workspace directories`.

**Cause:** two different things use the same word. The first is a folder that Windows will not let you write to. The second is a path outside the folders listed in `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`.

**Fix:** set `MCP_REVIT_WORKSPACE_DIR` to a folder you can write to, using an absolute path. List every folder you need in `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`, separated by semicolons. Restart the hub and your client. See the [configuration reference](configuration-reference.md).

**Look at:** the authenticated diagnostics command above.

### Add-in and server use different workspaces

**You see:** a snapshot id is returned but the server says `Snapshot '<id>' not found.`

**Cause:** the add-in and the Python server each have a workspace setting. If they differ, the snapshot is saved where the server does not look. A mismatch can still occur when environments or custom settings differ.

**Fix:** point both at the same folder, and restart Revit and the client.

---

## Install problems

### Windows or antivirus blocks the installer

**You see:** Windows SmartScreen says the publisher is unknown. Or your antivirus quarantines or blocks `AECModelBridge-Setup-<version>.exe`.

**Cause:** the installer is not code-signed yet. This is stated in the [install guide](install.md#download-the-installer). That is why SmartScreen warns. UNVERIFIED: whether a given antivirus product will flag it. That depends on the product.

**Fix:**

1. Download only from the [latest release](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/releases/latest).
2. Compare the file with the checksum in `SHA256SUMS.txt` on the same page. In PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\AECModelBridge-Setup-<version>.exe -Algorithm SHA256`.
3. If the hashes match, choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
4. If your antivirus blocks it, ask your IT team to allow it, or use the [source install](install.md#install-from-source).

If the hashes do not match, do not run the file. Report it.

**Copy to the bug report:** the antivirus product name, the exact warning text, and the hash you computed.

### Python or uv is missing for the uvx install

**You see:** the client says `uvx` is not found or is not recognized. Or Python is older than 3.11.

**Cause:** the one-click install buttons and the README entry run `uvx`, which comes with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). The package needs Python 3.11 or later. `uvx` also fetches the code from GitHub, so it needs Git.

**Fix:** install uv, close and reopen your client so it sees the new PATH, then retry. Check in a terminal: `uvx --version` and `git --version`. Or use the source install in [install](install.md#install-from-source), which uses a virtual environment.

### The MCP client cannot start the server

**You see:** the client shows the server as failed, stopped, or not connected. No tools appear.

**Cause (check in this order):**

1. The JSON config has a typo, such as a missing comma or a single backslash in a Windows path. Paths need `\\`.
2. The `command` is not found (see the entry above).
3. The server crashed at start. A bad value in an `MCP_REVIT_*` variable (for example a folder that does not exist in `MCP_REVIT_ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES`) is a likely cause. UNVERIFIED: not every bad value was tested.
4. The first `uvx` run is still downloading and the client timed out. UNVERIFIED: timeouts differ by client.

**Fix:** run the same command in a terminal and read the error. For a source install:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m revit_mcp_server.mcp_server
```

For the installer bundle, use its own interpreter: `C:\ProgramData\AECModelBridge\python\python.exe -m revit_mcp_server`. If you are on a release older than the fix for issue #159, `python\Scripts\aec-model-bridge.exe` (and the other `.exe` files in that folder) exits with code 1 and prints nothing, because pip wrote the build machine's path into them. Point your client at `python.exe` with the arguments `-m revit_mcp_server` instead, or install a release that ships the `.cmd` launchers.

A healthy server starts and waits silently for input. Press Ctrl+C to stop it. Then fix what the terminal showed, and restart the client.

**Copy to the bug report:** your config with any keys removed, and the terminal error.

### The add-in does not appear in Revit

**Cause:** the installed year does not match the Revit year, the manifest is missing, or Revit was open while you installed.

**Fix:** close Revit and run the installer again. Tick your Revit year. Look for `%APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\AECModelBridge.addin`. See [install](install.md#troubleshooting).

=== FILE: docs/error-catalogue.md ===

# Error catalogue

Errors and refusals that the AEC Model Bridge server returns to clients, with what to do about each.
This file is generated by `scripts/make_error_catalogue.py` from the source and from
`scripts/error_catalogue_notes.json`. Do not edit it by hand.

A tool failure reaches an MCP client in one of two shapes:

- The MCP layer refused or failed the call. The reply has `isError: true` and `structuredContent.error.kind` is a tool error kind.
- A module tool ran and returned `ok: false` with a result kind in `kind`, a `message` and a `hint`.

Refusals never change the model. A refused write needs a new plan that a person approves.
For logs and connection problems see [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

Entries: 153.

## Tool error kinds

Set by the MCP layer as `structuredContent.error.kind` when a call fails with `isError`. Entries: 13.

### `approval_blocked`

- When: The approval gate refused a call that changes the model: no approved plan, a plan that does not match, an expired approval, a policy rule, or a changed document.
- What to do: Read the message. Create a plan with plan_actions, ask the person to approve it, then run it with execute_plan. Do not retry the same call unchanged.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `bridge_error`

- When: The server could not reach Revit, lost the reply, or Revit ran the command and it failed.
- What to do: Run revit_health. Check that Revit is open with the add-in and a project loaded. After a failed write, read the attached result before planning again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `execution_error`

- When: A tool raised an error that is not one of the kinds above, for example bad arguments or a file problem.
- What to do: Read the message and fix the arguments. If it repeats with valid arguments, report a bug with the log (docs/troubleshooting.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `human_only`

- When: An AI client called approve_plan, reject_plan or rollback_plan.
- What to do: Stop. Ask the person to approve, reject or roll back the plan in the Revit panel or with the aec-model-bridge-approve command.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `input_needed`

- When: A tool needs one more input: an export without its output file, a level name that matches several levels, or a parameter name that does not exist but has close names. The client did not support elicitation, or the person declined, cancelled or did not answer in time.
- What to do: Read the message: it names the missing input and the choices. Call again with that input set. Do not guess a choice for the person.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `invalid_cursor`

- When: response_options.cursor was refused: it expired (default 600 seconds), the server restarted, it came from another call, or the tool takes no cursor.
- What to do: Call the tool again without a cursor and page from the new answer.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `invalid_response_options`

- When: The response_options argument is not an object, names an unsupported key, or has a value of the wrong type.
- What to do: Remove response_options or fix it as the message says, then call again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `policy_refused`

- When: The machine or workspace policy file turns off the tier of this tool (read, write, script or export), or the policy file is invalid and the tool is not a read.
- What to do: Use a tool of a tier that is on. To use this one, the person who manages the named policy file must change it, or switch on Dev mode in the panel (docs/security.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `rate_limited`

- When: Too many calls in a short time: the client session (default 600 per minute) or one tool (default 120 per minute for a write tool, 300 for a read tool) is over its limit. Nothing ran and no approved action was used. Approval tools are never counted.
- What to do: Wait the number of seconds in error.retry_after_seconds, then call again. Do not loop on the call. The person can change the limits with MCP_REVIT_RATE_LIMITS (docs/configuration-reference.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `task_not_supported`

- When: A tools/call carried a task field (MCP Tasks) for a tool that does not accept task-augmented calls. Nothing ran and no approved action was used.
- What to do: Call the tool without the task field, or use a tool whose execution.taskSupport is optional (docs/mcp-tasks.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `tool_profile_blocked`

- When: The tool is registered but this server's static MCP tool profile hides it.
- What to do: Use a tool the profile lists. To use this one, the person must change the tool profile and restart the server (docs/mcp-token-budget.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `tool_timeout`

- When: A read tool did not finish within its timeout (default 300 s) and was stopped. Nothing in the model changed. A write that runs out of time is not refused this way: it is reported as possibly still running and its approved action stays used.
- What to do: Ask for less (a narrower filter, fewer elements, a smaller view). The person can raise the timeout with MCP_REVIT_TOOL_TIMEOUT or MCP_REVIT_TOOL_TIMEOUTS (docs/configuration-reference.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

### `unknown_tool`

- When: The tool name is not registered in this server.
- What to do: Call tools/list and use an exact name. A module tool is missing when its module is off or failed to load.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`

## Result kinds

Set by module tools as `kind` in an `ok: false` result, next to `message`, `element_ids` and `hint`. Many tools share one kind. Entries: 112.

### `already_on_circuit`

- When: The element is already on a circuit that the tool did not make.
- What to do: The element is on a circuit this tool did not make. Remove it from that circuit in Revit first; this tool never moves elements between circuits. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `annotation_crop_unreadable`

- When: Revit gave no annotation crop for the reference view.
- What to do: Revit did not give the annotation crop of the reference view. Use annotation_crop on, off or keep instead.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `approval_required`

- When: A module write tool was called without an approved plan, or the approved action does not match the call.
- What to do: The approval gate refused the call. Nothing was sent to Revit.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `baseline_not_found`

- When: A comparison names a baseline snapshot that does not exist.
- What to do: List the saved baselines with the same tool, or take a new snapshot first. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`

### `baseline_not_saved`

- When: The baseline snapshot could not be written to the workspace.
- What to do: Check that the workspace folder is writable and has space, then take the snapshot again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`

### `binding_required`

- When: A recipe write was planned without the recipe version and sha256.
- What to do: Pass version and sha256 from revit_recipe_get (or a dry_run) so the approval covers exactly this code. Nothing was sent to Revit.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`

### `bindings_unreadable`

- When: Revit would not list the project's parameter bindings.
- What to do: Revit would not list the project's parameter bindings; nothing was changed. Check revit_health and try again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `bridge_error`

- When: The call to Revit failed: no connection, a lost reply or an expired request id.
- What to do: Run revit_health and check that Revit is running with the AEC Model Bridge add-in and a project open. After a write, check the model before repeating it.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_cleanup/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `category_mismatch`

- When: The family category does not fit the connector kinds of its ports.
- What to do: Use a category whose connectors fit the ports (mech: pipe/duct, plumb: pipe, air: duct, elec_eq/elec_fx/light: elec), or fix the port kinds. Nothing was sent to Revit.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `code_too_large`

- When: Recipe code is larger than 64 KiB.
- What to do: Shorten the recipe code to 64 KiB or less.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/recipe_store.py`

### `conflicting_values`

- When: One call gives the same element two different values for one parameter.
- What to do: The same element got two different values for one parameter (two items, or two instances of one type with scope 'type'). Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`

### `connector_in_use`

- When: The chosen connector is already connected.
- What to do: That connector is connected to something else. Choose another with near_m, sort or index. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `connector_not_found`

- When: No connector matches the filters.
- What to do: No connector matches the filters. Loosen diameter_mm, sort, index or near_m. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `crop_not_rectangular`

- When: The view crop region is not a rectangle.
- What to do: This tool copies and sets rectangular crop regions only. Reset the custom crop shape in Revit first.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `crossing_not_found`

- When: A crossing id is not in the current crossing list.
- What to do: Run revit_sparing_find with the same filters and use crossing_id values from its rows. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `document_mismatch`

- When: The active document is not the one the baseline was saved from.
- What to do: Open the model the baseline came from, or save a new baseline for this one.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`

### `domain_mismatch`

- When: The system or family does not belong to the tool's domain (pipe, duct, cable tray).
- What to do: The system and the tool do not belong together (or the family has connectors of another domain only). Pick a system of the tool's kind: pipe systems for pipes, air systems for ducts. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `dry_run_not_honoured`

- When: A dry run reported committed changes.
- What to do: A dry run reported committed changes. Check the elements with revit_get_parameters before doing anything else.

- When: The Revit add-in reported a script error before any result was produced.
- What to do: The add-in failed before the script produced a result. Read the message. For a write tool, check the model before repeating the call.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_cleanup/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_ifc/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `script_exception`

- When: The embedded script raised an exception inside Revit.
- What to do: A read-only call changed nothing. A write recipe may have committed changes before it failed: check the model before repeating it, and repeat it only through a new approved plan.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_cleanup/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_ifc/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `shared_parameter_file_missing`

- When: Revit has no shared parameter file set and none was passed.
- What to do: Point Revit at the firm's shared parameter file (Manage > Shared Parameters) or pass shared_parameter_file, then call again. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `sheet_not_found`

- When: No sheet has that number, or more than one does.
- What to do: Make the sheet first with revit_make_sheet, or check the number with revit_sheet_index. A number must match exactly one sheet.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `sheet_not_owned`

- When: The sheet was not made by this tool.
- What to do: Pass allow_foreign=true to add the schedule to a sheet this tool did not make.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `sheet_number_conflict`

- When: The table would give two sheets the same number.
- What to do: Choose numbers that no other sheet ends up with. This tool never renumbers sheets that are not in the table.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `starter_recipe`

- When: A built-in starter recipe was asked to be deleted or approved.
- What to do: Starter recipes are read only. Save your own recipe with the same id to replace one.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/recipe_store.py`

### `system_mismatch`

- When: The connectors belong to different systems, or the family has no connector of the system.
- What to do: Pick connectors or a system of the same domain, or fix the family. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `system_type_not_found`

- When: The route has no start connector and no system type exists.
- What to do: Start the route at a connector, or create the system type in Revit first. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `tee_needs_owned_trunk`

- When: A tee was asked for on a trunk the tool did not make.
- What to do: Use branch_to.route for a tee, or fitting 'takeoff' for a trunk given by ids. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `template_not_found`

- When: The view template name does not exist.
- What to do: Use one of the view template names listed in the message (revit_list_views_sheets_schedules with kinds ['templates']).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`

### `timeout_running`

- When: The wait for Revit ran out while the script was still running.
- What to do: Revit may still be running the script. Call revit_get_result with the request_id.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_cleanup/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_ifc/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_recipes/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `title_block_not_found`

- When: The title block type name does not exist.
- What to do: Use one of the title block type names listed in the message.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `too_many_elements`

- When: The call names more than 500 elements.
- What to do: At most 500 elements per call. Narrow the selectors or split the call. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_ifc/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`

### `too_many_hangers`

- When: The plan would place more hangers than max_hangers.
- What to do: Narrow the scope, or raise max_hangers (at most 500). Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `too_many_recipes`

- When: The workspace already holds the maximum number of recipes.
- What to do: Delete recipes you no longer need with revit_recipe_delete, then save again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/recipe_store.py`

### `too_many_sparings`

- When: The call would place more sparings than max_sparings.
- What to do: Narrow the call with level, system, ids or crossing_ids, or raise max_sparings (at most 500). Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `too_many_values`

- When: The call holds more parameter values than one call may carry.
- What to do: Split the call into smaller batches. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`

### `trunk_not_found`

- When: A branch names a trunk route or pipe that does not exist.
- What to do: Build the trunk route first (earlier in the same call, or an earlier call with the same tag), or list real pipe or duct ids. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `type_not_found`

- When: The pipe or duct type name does not exist.
- What to do: Use one of the pipe or duct type names listed in the message. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `unparsable_output`

- When: The script printed no summary the server can read.
- What to do: The add-in may run a different IronPython engine. Run revit_health, check the add-in version against the server, and report a bug if it persists.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_cleanup/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_ifc/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_params/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

### `view_already_placed`

- When: The view is already on another sheet.
- What to do: A view can be on one sheet only. Remove its viewport from the other sheet yourself or make a duplicate view first; this tool never moves a placed view.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `view_not_found`

- When: A view id or name does not exist.
- What to do: Check the view ids or names with revit_list_views_sheets_schedules.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `view_not_plan`

- When: A non-plan view was given to a tool that takes plan views.
- What to do: Only plan views take part. Pick floor, ceiling or area plans (revit_list_views_sheets_schedules).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `view_not_supported`

- When: The view type cannot hold revision clouds.
- What to do: Clouds go into plan, section and elevation views. Pick one of those.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_docs/module.py`

### `wrong_document`

- When: The active document is not the discipline model the tool needs.
- What to do: The bridge works on the active document only. Open the discipline model named in the message, make it the active document, and call again. Nothing was changed.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`, `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_sparing/module.py`

## Exception classes

Raised inside the server. The MCP layer turns most of them into one of the tool error kinds above, with the class message as text. Entries: 28.

### `ApprovalExpired`

- When: An approval or a drafted plan is older than approval_ttl.
- What to do: Create a new plan and ask the person to approve it. Nothing renews an old approval.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/approval.py`

### `ApprovalKeyError`

- When: The workspace approval signing key (plans/.keys/approval-signing.key) is a symlink, owned by another user, readable by others, or malformed. The approval was not recorded.
- What to do: Ask the person to delete the key file and approve the plan again. Plans approved under the old key must be approved again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/approval_signing.py`

### `AppsResourceError`

- When: A ui:// MCP Apps URI is unknown, names a plan that is not allowed or not found, or MCP_REVIT_MCP_APPS is off.
- What to do: Use ui://aec-model-bridge/plan-review or a plan id from list_pending_plans; check MCP_REVIT_MCP_APPS.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_apps.py`

### `BcfError`

- When: A BCF file or its path is unsafe or invalid: no workspace, path outside the workspace, bad zip entry or an oversized entry.
- What to do: Use a BCF file inside the workspace. Do not open archives from untrusted sources.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/bcf_exchange/module.py`

### `BridgeContractError`

- When: The payload for an add-in command does not match contracts/bridge-commands.json. Nothing was sent to Revit.
- What to do: Fix the parameter the message names and call again. MCP_REVIT_VALIDATE_BRIDGE_PAYLOADS=off turns the check off.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

### `BridgeError`

- When: Communication with the Revit bridge failed, or a tool reported a failure. Returned to clients as kind bridge_error.
- What to do: Run revit_health and check that Revit is running with the add-in.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

### `CassetteError`

- When: Replay mode cannot open, read or match a cassette, or MCP_REVIT_RECORD is not a plain cassette name. A kind of BridgeError, returned as bridge_error.
- What to do: Set MCP_REVIT_CASSETTE to a readable cassette file, record the session again for an unmatched request, or use a plain name (letters, digits, _ or -) for MCP_REVIT_RECORD. See docs/record-replay.md.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/bridge/cassette.py`

### `CategoryMismatch`

- When: A family spec uses a category that does not fit its port kinds.
- What to do: Pick a category that fits the port kinds or fix the ports. Nothing was sent to Revit.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_family/module.py`

### `CommandFailed`

- When: Revit ran the command and it failed. Only this error marks an in-flight approved action as failed.
- What to do: Read the attached result. Plan a corrected action; the old approval is used up.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

### `CursorError`

- When: A read cursor is malformed, unknown, expired, past the end or belongs to another call. Returned to clients as kind invalid_cursor.
- What to do: Call the tool again without a cursor, or repeat the first call's tool, arguments and fields exactly with the cursor.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/read_cursor.py`

### `DomainMismatch`

- When: A system belongs to a different domain than the tool's kind.
- What to do: Pick a system of the tool's kind, for example pipe systems for pipes.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/modules/revit_mep/module.py`

### `ElicitationForbidden`

- When: Server code tried to ask the person a question for an approval tool, from the approval code, or for something that looks like a secret.
- What to do: Nothing for the client. Plan approval comes only from a person in the panel or the CLI; this is a server bug if it is ever seen.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/elicitation.py`

### `HttpConfigError`

- When: MCP_REVIT_HTTP is on but the host is not loopback, the port is invalid, or MCP_REVIT_HTTP_TOKEN is missing or shorter than 16 characters. The server refuses to start.
- What to do: Fix the MCP_REVIT_HTTP_* settings, or unset MCP_REVIT_HTTP to use stdio.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/http_transport.py`

### `IncrementalMergeError`

- When: An incremental snapshot capture does not fit its base snapshot (another document, a cut-short capture, or an element missing from both).
- What to do: Nothing to do. snapshot_take catches it, takes a full snapshot and gives the reason in counts.incremental_reason.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/semantic/engine.py`

### `InputNeeded`

- When: A tool needs one more input from the person. The MCP layer asks through elicitation when the client supports it; otherwise it returns kind input_needed.
- What to do: Call again with the input the message names.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/elicitation.py`

### `InstanceRoutingError`

- When: A panel request cannot be routed to exactly one running Revit.
- What to do: Pass instance with the integer pid of the Revit process, or leave only one Revit open.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/panel_server.py`

### `PanelTokenError`

- When: The panel token file is unusable. The message never contains the token.
- What to do: Ask the person to restart the server and panel so a new token is written (docs/troubleshooting.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/panel_token.py`

### `PolicyError`

- When: The workspace policy file is invalid, or a plan breaks one of its rules. All writes are refused while the file is invalid.
- What to do: Change the plan to fit the policy, or ask the person to fix or relax the policy file (docs/security.md).
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/policy.py`

### `QueryError`

- When: A snapshot_compute pipeline is malformed: an unknown key, op, join or aggregate, a missing value, a bad 'from', or a limit exceeded. The message names the step.
- What to do: Fix the step the message names and call again. Nothing was read from Revit or written.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/semantic/compute.py`

### `ReadModeViolation`

- When: A script marked mode read contains something that could change the model.
- What to do: Remove the model-changing code, or run the script as a write that goes through a plan.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/read_mode.py`

### `RecipeError`

- When: A recipe request is refused. It carries a machine kind; those are listed under result kinds.
- What to do: Look up the kind in this file.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/security/recipe_store.py`

### `ResourceError`

- When: An MCP resource URI is unknown, malformed or names an id that is not allowed.
- What to do: List resources and use an exact URI.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/mcp_resources.py`

### `RevitMCPError`

- When: Base class of the server's own errors. Not raised directly.
- What to do: Handle the subclass named in the message.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

### `SchemaValidationError`

- When: Inputs failed the tool's declared JSON schema.
- What to do: Fix the argument the message names and call again.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

### `ToolProfileBlocked`

- When: A registered tool is hidden by the static MCP tool profile. Returned as kind tool_profile_blocked.
- What to do: Use a listed tool, or ask the person to change the profile.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/tool_profiles.py`

### `ToolTimedOut`

- When: Internal: a direct tool call outlived its timeout (call_limits.py). Never returned as is: a read becomes kind tool_timeout, a write becomes a reply that it may still be running.
- What to do: See mcp/tool_timeout. For a write, do not repeat the call; check the model with a read tool.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/call_limits.py`

### `UsageLockTimeout`

- When: Another server process held the tool usage counts lock (usage/.tool-usage.json.lock) for longer than the 2 s wait. Logged as a warning; it never fails a tool call.
- What to do: Nothing. The counts stay in memory and are written at the next flush. A lock file older than 30 s is removed as stale.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/usage_counts.py`

### `WorkspaceViolation`

- When: A tool targeted a path outside the allowed workspace directories, or a module wrote a file its manifest does not allow.
- What to do: Use a path inside the workspace (revit_get_context shows it). Do not try to reach other folders.
- Source: `packages/mcp-server-revit/src/revit_mcp_server/errors.py`

=== FILE: docs/adr/0008-approval-gate-lifecycle.md ===

# ADR 0008: Approval Gate & ActionPlan Lifecycle

## Status
Accepted. In 1.5.0. Bounded Revit 2024 read-only checks are recorded in the [live validation report](../revit-addin-live-validation-2026-10-14.md); approval execution, rollback and recovery still need live acceptance.

## Context
AI agents modifying production BIM models (e.g., Revit, Navisworks) pose significant risks of silent data corruption, coordinate drift, or breaking company standards. We need a secure boundary where AI agents can propose changes (read, analyze, and plan) and require explicit human review and approval in the default Ask first mode. Look only blocks changes; explicitly selected Dev or Auto permits unplanned writes under the limits below.

## Decisions

### 1. ActionPlan Lifecycle
An **ActionPlan** is the unit of human approval and execution control. It transitions through the following states:

```mermaid
---
config:
  look: neo
  theme: base
  themeVariables:
    primaryColor: "#334155"
    primaryTextColor: "#FFFFFF"
    primaryBorderColor: "#1E293B"
    secondaryColor: "#334155"
    tertiaryColor: "#334155"
    lineColor: "#6E7781"
    textColor: "#6E7781"
    titleColor: "#6E7781"
    nodeTextColor: "#FFFFFF"
    clusterBkg: "rgba(110,119,129,0.10)"
    clusterBorder: "#6E7781"
    edgeLabelBackground: "#334155"
    actorBkg: "#334155"
    actorTextColor: "#FFFFFF"
    actorBorder: "#1E293B"
    actorLineColor: "#6E7781"
    signalColor: "#6E7781"
    signalTextColor: "#6E7781"
    labelBoxBkgColor: "#334155"
    labelBoxBorderColor: "#6E7781"
    labelTextColor: "#FFFFFF"
    loopTextColor: "#6E7781"
    sequenceNumberColor: "#FFFFFF"
    noteBkgColor: "#F59E0B"
    noteTextColor: "#1F1300"
    noteBorderColor: "#92400E"
    transitionColor: "#6E7781"
    transitionLabelColor: "#FFFFFF"
    stateLabelColor: "#FFFFFF"
    stateBkg: "#334155"
    labelBackgroundColor: "#334155"
    compositeBackground: "#334155"
    specialStateColor: "#6E7781"
---
stateDiagram-v2
  state "Pending review" as Pending
  state "Rolled back" as RolledBack

  [*] --> Draft
  Draft --> Validated: plan_actions
  Validated --> Pending: submit
  Pending --> Approved: approve
  Pending --> Rejected: reject
  Approved --> Executed: execute
  Executed --> RolledBack: rollback_plan
  Rejected --> [*]
  RolledBack --> [*]

  classDef ok fill:#0F766E,stroke:#0B4F4A,color:#FFFFFF
  classDef blocked fill:#B91C1C,stroke:#7F1D1D,color:#FFFFFF
  class Approved,Executed ok
  class Rejected blocked
```

- **Draft**: A plan containing proposed actions (tool calls and arguments) under construction.
- **Validated**: The plan has been checked against schemas, and dry-run validation checks have run (e.g., uniqueness, category support, element ownership).
- **Pending**: Submitted to the human approval queue, visible on the dockable panel.
- **Approved**: Human checked the parameter diffs and element counts, giving explicit consent.
- **Rejected**: Human rejected the plan; it is closed and archived.
- **Executed**: The changes are applied to the model inside host transactions.
- **Rolled Back**: The recorded changes are reversed by `rollback_plan`, which applies inverse parameter values and can skip an action that has no recorded before-value. `rollback_plan` is for people only and has no panel button or `aec-model-bridge-approve` command yet. Revit's own Ctrl+Z, or a revert plan drafted with `plan_revert` and approved like any other plan, are the practical routes. None is verified in a live Revit session (UNVERIFIED).

### 2. ActionPlan Schema
The ActionPlan represents a batch of modifications:
```json
{
  "plan_id": "plan_01J...ULID",
  "state": "pending",
  "created_at": "2026-07-08T18:07:30Z",
  "actions": [
    {
      "action_id": "act_01...",
      "tool": "revit.batch_set_parameters",
      "arguments": {
        "elements": ["revit-uniqueid-1"],
        "parameter": "FireRating",
        "value": "60"
      },
      "diff": {
        "type": "parameter_change",
        "before": {"revit-uniqueid-1": {"FireRating": null}},
        "after": {"revit-uniqueid-1": {"FireRating": "60"}},
        "element_count": 1
      }
    }
  ],
  "is_reversible": true,
  "reversible_strategy": "inverse"
}
```

### 3. The Approval Gate Middleware
- **Enforcement Location**: The unified Python MCP hub acts as the single choke point.
- **Rule**: If `approval_mode` is `ask_first` (the default; `required` is the older name for the same mode), any tool call containing mutating or destructive metadata (`is_mutating=True` or `destructive=True`) must supply a valid, approved `plan_id`. Unplanned mutations are immediately blocked and returned as an authorization error.
- **Bound to the approved action** (approval v2): a call with a `plan_id` must match a not-yet-run action of that plan by tool name and canonical arguments (`plan_id`, `run_async`, `idempotency_key` are ignored; key order and `5` vs `5.0` do not matter). Only a `pending` plan can be approved; a `pending` or `approved` plan can be rejected, so a person can withdraw an approval before it runs.
- **Plan ids**: a `plan_id` must match `^plan_[0-9a-f]{12}$` and resolve to a file directly inside `<workspace>/plans` whose `plan_id` field matches. Anything else is refused.
- **Content binding**: `create_plan` stores `plan_hash` (SHA-256 over the plan id, creation time, snapshot, skipped list, and each action's id, tool, arguments and before value; plans that carry a `review` block, marked `hash_version: 2`, also cover the canonicalised review and `reverts_plan_id`). Approving requires `expected_hash`, the hash of the plan the person was shown (the command-line tool computes it from what it printed; the panel sends back the `plan_hash` from the list it rendered). `update_plan_state` refuses if the plan on disk does not have that hash, or no longer matches the hash stored at drafting, and stores `approved_hash`. Every execution path refuses an approved plan whose content no longer matches `approved_hash`.
- **Review block**: reviewable rationale (summary, reasoning, citations `{rule_id, clause, source}`, assumptions, excluded `{element_id, reason}`, warnings) goes in `review`, passed as `create_plan(review=...)` or the `plan_actions` `review` argument. It is strict (unknown keys refused, per-field length caps, 64 KB total), stored as given, hashed, and escaped by the command-line tool. Plans without a review keep hash version 1 and still verify; a plan mixing review and version is refused. Keys outside the hash (anything passed in `extra`, and lifecycle fields such as `state`, `approved_*`, `executed_at`, `results`) are metadata, not approved content, and `show` lists them. `plan_revert` writes conflicts, notes and warnings into `review`. The panel route sends a hub-validated `review_view` and the Plans view renders it; a v2 plan whose review cannot be shown (or that holds a credential-like value the panel would mask; paths, code and ordinary prose are shown as they are) has Approve disabled and points to `aec-model-bridge-approve show` (see docs/security.md, "Plan review in the panel").
- **Signed approval record** (issues #313, #314): `update_plan_state` is the only place an approval is recorded, for every channel, and it stores `approval_sig`, an HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical JSON encoding of `plan_id`, `approved_hash`, the approval state, `approved_via`, `approved_by`, `approved_at` and `binding` when present (`security/approval_signing.py`). The key is 32 bytes from `secrets.token_bytes`, made once per workspace at `plans/.keys/approval-signing.key` with mode 0600 (on Windows the workspace's user-profile location protects it; UNVERIFIED). Every path that relies on an approval (`verify_approved`, used by `execute_plan` and `claim_action`; rollback; `run_pyrevit_script`) refuses a missing or non-verifying signature with "This plan's approval record does not verify; approve it again.", plans approved before the change included. Comparison uses `hmac.compare_digest`. In configured or timed Auto the approval checks stay off, but a call with a `plan_id` still claims the matching action through `plans/.claims/`, and a call whose matching actions were all claimed before is refused, so an action runs at most once in every mode. Alternative considered: a key held only in server memory; rejected because the panel hub, the CLI and the MCP server are separate processes that must verify each other's approvals.
- **Still running is not done.** A tool that answers `{"status": "running", "request_id": ...}` (the add-in kept working past the soft wait) leaves its action `running` with the claim consumed. `ApprovalGate.mark_in_flight` writes `plans/.inflight/<request_id>.json` (plan id, action id, tool), so a restarted server still knows. When `revit_get_result` (or `revit_job_status` for a `revit_run_job` job, keyed `job_<id>`) returns a final result, `settle_in_flight` closes the action: `executed` on success, `failed` with Revit's message on failure. Only Revit's own verdict closes it; a lost connection or an expired id leaves it `running` for the human `recover` command. A late result never reopens or overwrites an action that is already closed or abandoned.
- **At most once**: every execution path (MCP, `run_async` at queue time, panel, chat, recipe and module steps, `execute_plan`) calls `ApprovalGate.claim_action` before the tool runs. Under a per-plan lock (a thread lock plus a file lock), it checks the plan, finds the open action and creates `plans/.claims/<plan_id>.<action_id>` with `O_EXCL`, then marks the action `running`. When the tool reports final success, the action becomes `executed`; a final failure becomes `failed` and stays consumed. A `running` result remains in flight as described above. When no action is open or running, the plan becomes `executed` (all succeeded) or `partial`. A failed action needs a new plan.
- **Humans approve**: `approve_plan`, `reject_plan` and `rollback_plan` stay registered but are not listed to MCP clients and are refused by the shared dispatch (`security/dispatch.py`) used by MCP, the panel chat, module tool executors and the panel route, and by `ApprovalProvider.execute_tool` itself. A plan cannot contain them. They run only through `ApprovalProvider.execute_human_tool`, which the panel route calls with `via="panel"`, or through the command-line tool (`via="cli"`). The panel exposes approve/reject, and the command-line tool has no rollback command; use Revit Ctrl+Z or an approved `plan_revert` for everyday reversal. The channel is set by the route; `approver`/`approved_via` arguments are ignored and `approved_by` is the OS account of the approving process.
- **`approval_mode`**: the value is trimmed and lower-cased and is one of `look_only`, `ask_first` (alias `required`) or `auto`. Effective `auto` permits unplanned writes, either from the configured Auto mode or a signed panel override; Dev still validates any supplied plan id (see ADR 0018 below). `look_only` refuses every tool that changes the model, on every path, including `rollback_plan`. Unknown values behave as `ask_first` and log a warning.
- **Limits**: none of this authenticates the human. A process that can run shell commands as the user can run the command-line tool with `--yes`. The panel's `/execute` endpoint authenticates a local process, not a person: it relies on the Host/Origin/Content-Type checks and on a per-user token file (see [security](../security.md)), and any process running as the same user can read that token. Software with write access to `<workspace>/plans` can replace a plan together with its stored hashes or remove claim files.
- **Explicit Dev exception**: the confirmed panel switch persists across restarts through an HMAC-signed workspace record and an owner-only nonce authority. Switching off revokes that authority; replaying an old record cannot re-enable Dev. It permits unplanned writes, while configured Look only, human-only tool restrictions, Python read-mode guards, sandbox and redaction remain enforced. A supplied plan id still requires an unchanged, unused approved action. Dev calls and switches are audited; audit failure refuses the call, and one authorization snapshot binds a mutating call to its audit and plan checks. See [ADR 0018](0018-explicit-development-mode.md).
- **Pending only in the panel**: the panel's Plans list is fed by `ApprovalGate.list_pending_plans`, so it shows only plans in the `pending` state. `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` works for plans in any state (`list` covers pending plans only). `proofs/<plan_id>.json` exists only for executed (or attempted) plans; approved-but-unexecuted and rejected plans have no proof bundle.
- **Auto-Approval**: For headless CI/CD pipelines, `approval_mode=auto` can be set via environment variable (`MCP_REVIT_APPROVAL_MODE=auto`).

### 4. Rollback Strategies
- **Revit Undo (`undo`)**: Built for batchable plans (#294). When every action is a plain model write on the plan-batch list (parameter writes, moves, rotations) and the add-in lists `revit.execute_plan_batch`, `execute_plan` sends the whole plan in one request. The add-in runs it in one ExternalEvent turn inside one `TransactionGroup` named `"AEC Model Bridge: <plan title> (<short id>)"`, each action in its own transaction, and assimilates the group into one undo step. It stops at the first failure and rolls the group back. Every action is still claimed before the request and its outcome is recorded from the per-action results. Other plans run one transaction per action, so undoing them takes one Ctrl+Z per action. Live-Revit behaviour is UNVERIFIED.
- **Rolled-back preview (`rollback_preview`)**: Built for the same plans (#293). When the add-in lists `revit.preview_plan_batch`, `plan_actions` sends the draft actions to it before the plan is saved. The add-in runs them in one `TransactionGroup` that it always rolls back and reports the changed element ids, each action's outcome and the Revit warnings. The server stores the record on the plan inside the hashed content, so it cannot change after approval and a changed model needs a new draft. The CLI `show` and the panel list it. It is not an approval and not an execution: nothing is claimed, no proof is written and no plan state changes. If the add-in says the preview was not rolled back, the plan is shown as not approvable. No preview is taken in mock mode, with an older add-in, in look-only mode or for tools outside the plan-batch list; the plan is then drafted as before. Live-Revit behaviour is UNVERIFIED.
- **Inverse Counter-Plan (`inverse`)**: For persistent history rollbacks, the hub records the before-state (e.g., parameter values) and `rollback_plan` writes those values back in reverse order. An action with no recorded before-value (including an empty one) is skipped and reported as a warning, so a rollback can be partial. `plan_revert` drafts the same reversal as a new plan that needs approval. Live-Revit behaviour is UNVERIFIED.
- **Irreversible (`none`)**: High-risk operations (e.g., deleting models, file outputs) cannot be rolled back. A separate second confirmation for them is planned, not built: today they go through the same single approval as any other plan.

## Consequences
- **Trust & Safety**: Reduces the risk of hallucinated or malicious AI writes damaging BIM models. The gate is enforced in the hub; behaviour in a live Revit session is UNVERIFIED.
- **Audit Trails**: In Ask first mode, each approved write corresponds to a versioned ActionPlan, an approving OS account and an audit ledger entry. Dev permits unplanned writes and separately audits its calls and switches; the account does not prove a person is present.
- **Decoupled Orchestration**: AI agents can generate plans asynchronously while running long-running processes (e.g., clash detection), leaving the execution to the user.

=== FILE: docs/security.md ===

# Security model

Bounded Revit 2024 read-only checks ran on 14 October 2026; see the [live validation record](revit-addin-live-validation-2026-10-14.md). Mutating acceptance, recovery and multi-instance routing remain unverified. The [release checklist](release-checklist.md) tracks the remaining checks.

AEC Model Bridge uses several layers to protect your models and files from unwanted or destructive actions by AI agents. The layers are: clear trust boundaries, loopback-only connections, a workspace sandbox, input checks, an approval step for changes, and audit logs.

---

## 1. Trust boundaries and architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  External client / LLM Agent (Untrusted)                    │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                      │ MCP Protocol (stdio JSON-RPC)
                      ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Unified Python MCP Server (Router)                         │
│  - Configures environment & paths                           │
│  - Enforces workspace sandbox via WorkspaceMonitor          │
│  - Redacts sensitive logs & captures audits                 │
│  - Routes tool calls to in-process or loopback providers    │
└──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────┘
           │          │          │          │          │
   Local C#│   Local C#│  Headless│  In-Proc │   Cloud  │
   Bridge  │   Bridge  │  IFC     │  Helper  │   OAuth  │
   (:3000) │   (:3004) │  (Python)│  (SQLite)│  (HTTPS) │
           ▼          ▼          ▼          ▼          ▼
┌──────────┐┌─────────┐┌─────────┐┌─────────┐┌──────────┐
│  Revit   ││  Rhino  ││ IfcOpen ││ AEC     ││ Speckle  │
│  Add-in  ││  Bridge ││ Shell   ││ Mapper  ││ & APS    │
└──────────┘└─────────┘└─────────┘└─────────┘└──────────┘
```

The Revit add-in listens on port `3000` only in legacy mode. In the default mode it picks a dynamic port (see section 2).

The system has these parts:
1. **Unified Python MCP server**: the central gateway. It runs on your machine and talks to the AI client over standard input and output (stdio).
2. **Revit add-in**: runs inside Revit and opens a local HTTP port.
3. **Rhino bridge add-in**: runs inside Rhino and opens HTTP port 3004.
4. **IFC parsing**: runs inside the Python server with `IfcOpenShell`. Revit is not needed.
5. **Speckle and APS cloud connections**: call external APIs over HTTPS with OAuth-PKCE.

---

## 2. Network security and the local boundary

All desktop bridges listen on the loopback address only.

### Localhost boundary
- Add-ins bind to `127.0.0.1` (localhost) only.
- They reject connections from other machines.
- Never expose them through a public reverse proxy or port forwarding.

### Authentication modes (Revit add-in)
The C# Revit bridge has two modes:
1. **Contract v2 mode (default)**: the add-in picks a dynamic loopback port and creates a random bearer token each session. It writes both to a local registry file. The Python MCP server reads that file and sends the token with every request.
2. **Legacy mode (opt-in)**: set the add-in's environment variable `MCP_REVIT_LEGACY_PORT` to `true` or `1`. The add-in then binds to fixed port `3000` with no authentication and relies only on the localhost boundary. Use it only if an older client needs it.

### Named-pipe transport (opt-in, UNVERIFIED)
Any local process, including one of another Windows user, can connect to a loopback port. With `AEC_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT=pipe` set for Revit, the add-in also opens a named pipe whose ACL allows only the current Windows user, and publishes its name as `pipe_name` in the registry entry. With `MCP_REVIT_BRIDGE_TRANSPORT=pipe` the Python server sends requests over that pipe, with the same JSON and the same session token. The client refuses a pipe that is not served by the Revit process in the registry entry. The HTTP port stays open in this release, so the pipe does not yet remove the loopback exposure. If the selected entry has no pipe, the server warns and uses HTTP. The pipe ACL and live behaviour are UNVERIFIED in a live Windows session. See [ADR 0021](adr/0021-named-pipe-transport.md).

### Streamable HTTP transport (opt-in)
The MCP server speaks stdio by default and opens no port. Setting `MCP_REVIT_HTTP=1` makes it serve MCP over Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` instead, for clients that accept only an HTTP server. It serves the same tools from the same registry and the same approval gate as stdio; it adds no write path.

Threat model:
