- A request with no recorded match fails with: `Replay: cassette '<name>' has no recorded response for command '<command>' with these parameters.` Record the session again or add the line by hand.
- A recorded error is raised again: `CommandFailed` for a failed command, `BridgeError` otherwise.
- Without `MCP_REVIT_CASSETTE`, or with a file that cannot be read or parsed, every call fails with a plain error that names the problem.
- `revit_get_context` reports mock-style context in replay mode, because no Revit session exists. `revit_list_commands` is not available.
- Write tools still go through `plan_actions`, approval and `execute_plan`. A write in replay only returns the recorded response; nothing changes in any model.

## Use a cassette as a regression test

The test suite has a `cassette_replay` fixture (`packages/mcp-server-revit/tests/conftest.py`, helper in `tests/cassette_replay.py`):

```python
from pathlib import Path

CASSETTE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "cassettes" / "walls-check.jsonl"


def test_walls_check_still_replays(cassette_replay):
    cassette_replay(CASSETTE)
```

For each line with a `tool`, the helper calls that tool through the Revit provider in replay mode. The provider builds the bridge request again from the recorded arguments, so a changed payload builder fails with "no recorded response". The tool output must equal the recorded response; pass `compare=False` for tools that change the add-in result (for example paged reads). Lines without a tool, or with `arguments_redacted`, are replayed at bridge level only. Recorded errors must be raised again. Every line must be used.

`tests/fixtures/cassettes/sample_session.jsonl` is a small hand-written example.

## Limits

- Recording sees what the provider sends through the bridge client. `/health` probes are not recorded.
- Masking happens before matching, so two requests that differ only in a masked value (two different paths) match the same line.
- Live-Revit recording is UNVERIFIED: the recorder is tested with a stand-in bridge client, not against a running Revit.

## Related

- [Configuration reference](configuration-reference.md)
- [Logging and audit](logging-and-audit.md)
- [Privacy](privacy.md)

=== FILE: docs/release-checklist.md ===

# Release checklist

Ordered list for shipping from `dev` to `main`. Section 2 has no PASS or FAIL recorded. Bounded read-only Revit 2024 checks passed; see [the live validation report](revit-addin-live-validation-2026-10-14.md). Mutating acceptance and other Revit years are UNVERIFIED. Known limits are in section 3 and in [security.md](security.md).

## 0. Release flow

- Open one release PR into `main` from `dev`, or from a `release/*` branch of this repository when `dev` conflicts with `main`. Merge it with a merge commit.
- `dev` is frozen while that PR is open. PRs into `dev` wait until it lands. The `release-freeze` workflow fails on PRs into `dev` while a PR into `main` is open whose head is `dev` or a `release/*` branch of this repository; add `release-freeze` as a required check on `dev`.
- Tag after the release PR is merged, from the merge commit on `main`.
- Issues fixed on `dev` carry the `fixed-in-dev` label and close when the release reaches `main`.

## 1. What CI proves

The workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push and pull request, and nightly. Pull requests run Python on Windows 3.11 and Ubuntu 3.13 and build the add-ins only when their C# folders change. Pushes to `main` and `dev`, the nightly run and manual runs use the full matrix (Windows 3.11, 3.12, 3.13; Ubuntu 3.12, 3.13) and every build. It proves:

- Python lint (`ruff check`), the Python test suite with coverage, version consistency (`scripts/version.py check`), changelog fragments (`scripts/changelog.py check`), tool count claims (`scripts/sync_counts.py --check`), `llms-full.txt` freshness, `uv.lock` freshness and tool catalog generation.
- Repository metadata validation, wheel and sdist build, `twine check --strict`, and a smoke test of the built wheel in a clean venv.
- The Revit add-in and the Rhino bridge add-in compile (`dotnet build`).
- Workflow files pass `actionlint`.
- The doc tests, including the translated READMEs and install links, pass.

CI does not start Revit. Tests that touch Revit use mock providers.

## 2. Needs a live Revit

Run on a Windows machine with Revit, starting with the write test in section 5. Mark each PASS or FAIL.

1. First real write (for example `revit_set_parameter_value` through an approved plan). A crash here is the most important finding.
2. Undo behaviour. A plan of only parameter writes, moves and rotations runs as one `revit.execute_plan_batch` and should be one Ctrl+Z step named "AEC Model Bridge: <plan title> (<short id>)" (UNVERIFIED). Check it with a plan of two or more actions, check that a plan whose second action fails leaves the model unchanged, and check that other plans still take one Ctrl+Z per action. Check `rollback_plan`, which can skip actions that have no recorded before-value.
2a. Rolled-back preview (UNVERIFIED). Draft a plan of two parameter writes with `plan_actions`. The plan should carry `rollback_preview` with the changed element ids, the before and after values and any Revit warnings, and `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` and the panel should list it. Check that the model, the undo stack and the parameter values are unchanged after drafting, that a preview with a failing second action leaves the model unchanged, and that a plan with another tool drafts without a preview.
3. Two Revits open at once: requests reach the Revit the person means ([ADR 0014](adr/0014-multi-revit-routing.md), the "Several Revits" section of security.md). Also draft a plan in Revit A and run it in Revit B with the same file open: it must be refused as a different Revit process (issue #152, UNVERIFIED). Record the Revit version and commit.
4. The WebView2 panel loads, lists pending plans and approves one. Run `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` for the same plan and compare it with what the panel showed.
5. Windows ACL on `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AECModelBridge\panel-hub.token`: only the current user has access. Windows does not re-verify the ACL on read.
6. The Revit 2024 Release build and authenticated panel backend passed on 14 October 2026. Build and run the net8 and net10 targets as well, and repeat the release checks on each supported year.
7. Verify the panel review card and explicit Dev mode (Settings, Dev mode). Dev must stay visibly enabled until switched off, audit its writes, and preserve read-mode guards, filesystem scope and supplied-plan checks.
8. Image return (issue #211, UNVERIFIED). Call `revit_export_image` with `return_image: true` on a view that has been opened. The result should hold the JSON text and one PNG image block, and the file should stay in the workspace. Then export a large view (more than 2 MB) and check the refusal names the 2 MB cap.

Results for 1.6.0, Revit 2026.5, scratch copy of the Snowdon Towers sample, 2026-11-26:
- 1 PASS: a two-action `revit_set_parameter_value` plan, approved by the person in the panel, wrote both values. No crash.
- 2 PASS for the batched case: the plan ran as one batch, reported `undo.one_step: true`, and one Ctrl+Z restored both values. The failing-second-action case and `rollback_plan` were not run.
- 2a PASS: drafting carried a rolled-back preview and left the parameter values unchanged.
- 4 PASS: the panel listed and approved the plan. Findings: #383 (plans from other documents listed), #384 (review card fields unknown).
- 7 PARTIAL: Dev switches on and off and is shown in the panel. Findings: #385 (audit logs read polls). Writes in Dev were not run.
- 3, 5 and 6 not run. Revit 2027 is UNVERIFIED. Other findings: #386 to #390.
- Fixed after the live run, UNVERIFIED in Revit: #388 (IronPython 3.4.2 for Revit 2026 on .NET 10), #389, #390, #386, #383, #384, #387, #385.
- New ribbon (#395) and panel (#400): the look inside Revit and WebView2 is UNVERIFIED. Check both themes, the Connection toggle and slide-out, and that the panel fonts load.

## 3. Known limits (from security.md)

- Plans do not record the Revit that created them. Until fixed, a plan drafted in Revit A can run against Revit B.
- The client sends the raw token to whatever listens on 127.0.0.1:8787. On a shared machine another user could bind the port first.
- The hub caps request threads at `AEC_PANEL_MAX_THREADS` (default 32) and keeps 2 for `/execute`; over the cap a connection gets 503 with `Retry-After: 1` and no thread. Slow clients can still fill the other slots for up to 30 s per blocking read and delay non-`/execute` panel routes (UNVERIFIED with the live panel). MCP tool calls have per-tool timeouts and rate limits (UNVERIFIED in live Revit; see configuration-reference.md).
- Routed bridge clients: the routing lock no longer covers network calls, and a cached client is dropped when its Revit registry entry is gone or its `/health` fails three times in a row after failed calls. Tested with fakes only; UNVERIFIED with two live Revits.
- The dev panel displays validated plan reviews and blocks approval when a review is malformed, unsupported or too large. These browser checks passed; live plan approval acceptance remains pending. Compare the card with `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` before approving.
- The panel Plans view lists pending plans only. `aec-model-bridge-approve show <plan_id>` works for a plan in any state; `proofs/` bundles exist only for plans that were executed or attempted.
- One-step undo covers only plans made of parameter writes, moves and rotations, run through `revit.execute_plan_batch` (UNVERIFIED in live Revit). Other plans undo with Ctrl+Z once per action. A revert plan (`plan_revert`) is approved like any other plan. `rollback_plan` is for people only and has no panel button or command-line command yet.
- Executing a plan costs O(n^2) in its action count; keep plans to a few hundred actions.
- Environment Auto, timed panel Auto and explicit panel Dev skip per-change approval. Dev has no expiry until switched off and applies across sessions sharing the workspace; it does not relax filesystem scope or read-mode guards. An explicitly supplied plan must still be valid and approved.
- The panel's `/execute` endpoint and the approval command line authenticate a local process, not a person. Do not give an AI client a shell on the same account if you rely on the gate.
- Write access to the workspace defeats the hash check.
- `plan_actions` captures a before-value only for `revit_set_parameter_value`.
- Some Navisworks and proxy tools may still be ungated; `revit_calculate_material_quantities` is ungated although the add-in marks it mutating (UNVERIFIED).
- Reject any pending revert plan drafted before upgrading.
- Cerberus is a planned feature inside AEC Model Bridge. It is not built.

## 4. Steps only the maintainer can do

1. Open the pull request from `dev` to `main` and review it. Do not merge until sections 1 and 2 are done or their gaps are accepted in writing.
2. Import the repository rulesets in GitHub settings.
3. Upload `docs/images/readme/social-preview.png` under repository Settings, General, Social preview. Only an admin can set it.
4. Enable the docs site: repository Settings, Pages, Build and deployment, Source: GitHub Actions. `.github/workflows/docs.yml` then deploys the MkDocs site on the next push to `main` that touches `docs/` or `mkdocs.yml` (or run the workflow by hand). Until then the deploy job fails and the site is not published.
5. Enable Discussions and create the categories in [maintainer/discussions.md](maintainer/discussions.md).
6. Have counsel review the licences and the rule packs ([rule-packs.md](rule-packs.md), [LICENSING.md](../LICENSING.md)).
7. Have native speakers review the 16 translated READMEs in `docs/i18n/`, including the Plans view note, approval and undo wording, and the current screenshot alt text. Source corrections do not establish native-language review.
8. Run a pilot with BIM coordinators. None has been run yet.
9. Tag and publish the release ([versioning.md](versioning.md)).

## 5. Minimal safe write test

The first real write against Revit since the `CreateTransaction` fix (#95). Builds without that fix could recurse until Revit crashed. Save other Revit sessions first. Use a scratch copy of a small model, never a project file.

1. Open the copy, close other Revit documents, and take a snapshot (`revit_extract_snapshot`).
2. Pick one element with an editable text parameter, for example a door's `Comments`. Note its element id and value.
3. Ask the assistant to plan exactly one `revit_set_parameter_value` (parameter `Comments`, value `dev-test-1`) with `plan_actions`. Do not let it execute. Dev and timed Auto must be off; approval mode must be `ask_first`.
4. In the Revit panel, check the arguments match what you asked for, then Approve. (Or `aec-model-bridge-approve`.)
5. Ask the assistant to run `execute_plan`.
6. Read the parameter in the Properties palette. Pass: value is `dev-test-1` and Revit did not hang or crash. Fail: freeze, close, a panel error, or an unchanged value.
7. Press Ctrl+Z once and read it again. Pass: the original value is back. If it took more steps, note how many. A one-action plan is one step either way; repeat with a two-action plan to check the one-step plan undo.
8. Record pass or fail for the write and for undo, any message text, and the lines in `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\bridge.jsonl` around that time.

Stop and report if step 5 or 6 fails.

## 6. Known limits of the dev drop

Accepted for now. Check they behave as described; do not report them as new findings. Limits already in section 3 are not repeated.

- The panel hub token authenticates a process, not a person. Any program running as your Windows user can read `panel-hub.token` and call `/execute`, including to approve a plan. The Host and Origin checks only stop browser pages.
- Approvals are not bound to a document or a view and never expire. A plan approved on one model can run after you switch documents if the element ids and arguments still match. Reject plans you no longer want.
- An action can stay `running` if the submit to Revit fails part-way or the process dies. It is consumed and will not rerun. After checking in Revit what it changed, abandon it with `aec-model-bridge-approve recover <plan_id> --reason "..."` and ask for a new plan.
- Navisworks and proxy tools: #105 gated five tools, not every mutating one.
- The add-in snapshot extractor does not fill every field, so several checks report "not enough data".
- The command line does not authenticate who is typing. A program that can run shell commands as you can run `aec-model-bridge-approve approve <id> --yes`.
- One hub serves all Revits. A plan drafted in one can be executed against another.
- Rollback can skip actions and only handles parameter writes.

## 7. Registries and stores

Nothing here is automated except the workflows named. Account steps belong to the maintainer.

| Target | How | State |
|---|---|---|
| Official MCP Registry | `server.json` is the source. `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` publishes with GitHub OIDC when a release is published or on manual dispatch. Manual: `mcp-publisher login github`, `mcp-publisher publish`, after `mcp-publisher validate`. | Configured. Update `server.json` version, artifact URL and SHA-256 when the `.mcpb` changes. |
| PyPI | `.github/workflows/publish-pypi.yml` builds the wheel and sdist from the stable tag and publishes with Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no token) in the `pypi` environment. `release.yml` dispatches it after it creates a non-prerelease release; it also runs on `release: published` and by hand (`workflow_dispatch` with `tag`). Pre-release tags are refused. One-time setup is in [PyPI trusted publisher](#pypi-trusted-publisher). The `mcp-name` marker is in `packages/mcp-server-revit/README.md`. | Not published. Build, `twine check --strict` and a clean-venv install passed. |
| VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX | `.github/workflows/vscode-extension.yml` publishes when a non-pre-release GitHub release tag equals the extension version. Secrets: `VSCE_PAT`, `OVSX_PAT`. A store with no secret is skipped. Publisher and namespace `Sam-AEC` must exist. | Not published. Edit the extension README section "Build and install locally" before the first release. |
| winget | Templates in `packaging/winget/manifests/`, filled by `packaging/winget/fill_manifests.py <version>` from the published installer and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The maintainer submits with `wingetcreate`; see [winget.md](winget.md). | Not submitted. |
| GitHub MCP Registry, VS Code gallery | Read from the official registry. `.vscode/mcp.json` gives a workspace install. | Follows the official registry. |
| Claude Code plugin | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `packages/claude-plugin/`. Users run `/plugin marketplace add Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge`, then `/plugin install aec-model-bridge@aec-model-bridge`. Schema UNVERIFIED against `claude plugin validate`. | In the repository only. |
| Anthropic directory | Local `.mcpb` listings are reported as no longer accepted (UNVERIFIED); a local server goes in as a plugin through the developer portal. Needs the privacy policy in `privacy.md` (referenced from `manifest.json`). | Not submitted. |
| Glama | `glama.json` at the repository root on `main`; claim ownership while signed in as `Sam-AEC`. Re-claim after changing the file. The file lists maintainers only; the listing text is reported to come from the repository About text and README (UNVERIFIED), so those must say mock mode runs without Revit and live use needs Windows, Revit 2024 to 2027 and the add-in. | Not claimed. |
| Smithery | `smithery.yaml` builds the root `Dockerfile` in mock mode only. Its config description says mock mode runs without Revit and live use needs Windows, Revit 2024 to 2027 and the add-in. | Not listed. |
| Cline marketplace | Issue in the Cline marketplace repository with a 400x400 logo (none in the repo). Process UNVERIFIED. | Not submitted. |
| Other directories (PulseMCP, MCP.Directory, MCP.so) | Submit the repository URL; they read the README and registry data. | Not submitted. |

### PyPI trusted publisher

Do once, signed in to pypi.org and GitHub as the maintainer. Nothing in the repository can do these steps.

1. On GitHub: Settings, Environments, New environment, name `pypi`. Under deployment branches and tags, choose "Selected branches and tags" and add the tag rule `v*`. Optional: add yourself as a required reviewer, so each upload waits for a click.
2. On pypi.org: Account settings, Publishing, "Add a new pending publisher" (the project does not exist yet), GitHub tab. Enter PyPI project name `aec-model-bridge`, owner `Sam-AEC`, repository `aec-model-bridge`, workflow name `publish-pypi.yml`, environment name `pypi`. After the first upload the pending publisher becomes a normal trusted publisher on the project.
3. Check: run `publish-pypi.yml` by hand with the latest stable tag, or wait for the next stable release. A wrong environment or workflow name fails at the upload step with `invalid-publisher`.

The environment name on PyPI and in the workflow must match. If an older pending publisher exists with no environment, delete it and add the one above.

### GitHub environments

- `release`: deployment branches and tags limited to `v*` tags. `release.yml`, `publish-mcp.yml` and the publish job of `vscode-extension.yml` use it, so a manual run from a branch cannot reach OIDC or store tokens. Rebuild an existing tag with `gh workflow run release.yml --ref vX.Y.Z -f tag=vX.Y.Z`; `release.yml` refuses a manual run on a branch. A dry run with the `ref` input is also dispatched on a tag.
- `maintenance`: deployment branches limited to `main`. `rulesets-drift.yml` uses it, so `SCORECARD_TOKEN` is not exposed to other branches.

### OpenSSF Scorecard

`.github/workflows/scorecard.yml` runs weekly and on pushes to `main`, uploads results to code scanning and publishes them to the Scorecard API for the README badge. The badge shows "invalid" until the first run on `main` completes.

claude.ai on the web and phones accepts only remote HTTPS connectors, so it cannot reach a local Revit.

Release steps: run `python scripts/changelog.py build --version X.Y.Z` first (folds `changes/*.md` into the release section), then bump versions as in [versioning.md](versioning.md), attach the `.mcpb` and installer to the GitHub release (`scripts/version.py` keeps plugin and marketplace versions in step), update `server.json`, run `mcp-publisher validate`, publish, then check discovery through the registry API.

GitHub releases and tags v0.1.0 to v1.1.0 were deleted on 2026-10-09. The code stays in git history, and the MCP Registry still lists 1.0.1, 1.0.2 and 1.1.0 with dead download links. Releases v1.2.1 to v1.3.3 carry GPL-3.0 licence files in tag, wheel and `.mcpb`.

## 8. Self-hosted nightly live test

`.github/workflows/live-nightly.yml` is optional. It needs a Windows machine with Revit and a self-hosted runner. Nothing in CI starts Revit, so this is the only automated live check. It has no PASS or FAIL recorded yet; the first runs are UNVERIFIED.

What a run does:

1. Copies the canonical model to a scratch file with `-scratch-` in its name and opens it in a fresh Revit (`scripts/revit/nightly/prepare-scratch.ps1`). It refuses to start when a Revit is already open.
2. Runs the read-only add-in benchmark (`scripts/bench-addin.ps1`).
3. Checks the live context: the scratch title and GUID match, approval mode is Ask me first, Dev is off.
4. Takes a snapshot, drafts one `revit_set_parameter_value` plan, checks that `execute_plan` refuses it while pending, approves it bound to its hash, executes it, and compares a second snapshot (one modified element).
5. Drafts the revert with `plan_revert`, approves and executes it, then checks the original value and an empty snapshot comparison.
6. Writes `artifacts/revit-nightly/<run id>.json` with PASS, FAIL or NOT_RUN per check, timings in ms and the benchmark, and uploads it as the `live-nightly-report` artifact. Then it closes Revit and deletes the scratch copy.

The runner approves its own plans through the panel route, because nobody is present at night. This tests the gate and the write path on a scratch model. It does not replace the human approval check in section 5. The run fails if the gate lets an unapproved plan execute.

Setup, once, by the maintainer:

1. Install the runner on the machine under the Windows account that runs Revit. Add the labels `self-hosted`, `windows` and `revit-live`. Run it as a normal user process, not as a service on another account, because Revit and the panel token are per user.
2. Install uv and Python 3.11 or newer. Install the add-in and check that the panel hub answers on `127.0.0.1:8787`.
3. Generate the canonical model ([canonical model README](../packages/mcp-server-revit/tests/fixtures/canonical-model/README.md)) and save it outside the repository. Note its `CreationGUID` and the id of an element with an editable `Comments` parameter.
4. Set these repository variables (they hold no secrets): `AEC_NIGHTLY_MODEL_PATH`, `AEC_NIGHTLY_REVIT_EXE`, `AEC_NIGHTLY_MODEL_GUID`, `AEC_NIGHTLY_ELEMENT_ID`.
5. Use the runner for this repository only, and never for pull requests. The workflow has no `pull_request` trigger and runs only from `dev` or `main`. Do not enable "Run workflows from fork pull requests" for self-hosted runners.
6. Run the workflow by hand once and read the report. Disable the workflow to stop the nightly runs.

Details and limits: `scripts/revit/nightly/README.md`.

=== FILE: docs/versioning.md ===

# Versioning and releases

AEC Model Bridge follows [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org). The version is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, and release tags are the same number with a `v` in front: `v1.3.0`.

One file decides the version: [`VERSION`](../VERSION) in the repository root. Everything else is generated from it, so the Revit add-in, the MCP server, the installer and the registry listing can never disagree.

## What each number means

| Bump | Use it when | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **MAJOR** | A tool is removed or renamed, a tool's arguments change in a way that breaks existing prompts or recipes, or a supported Revit version is dropped. | `1.3.0` to `2.0.0` |
| **MINOR** | You add tools, workflows, UI, a new Revit version, or a new provider. Existing behaviour keeps working. | `1.2.1` to `1.3.0` |
| **PATCH** | Bug fixes, CI fixes, documentation and security patches with no new features. | `1.3.0` to `1.3.1` |

Pre-releases use a hyphen suffix: `1.4.0-rc.1`, `1.4.0-beta.2`. GitHub marks them as pre-releases automatically. The Python wheel is named with the PEP 440 form (`1.4.0rc1`); `build-release.ps1` converts it for you.

## Where the version lives

`scripts/version.py` keeps these in sync:

| File | Field |
|---|---|
| `VERSION` | the source of truth |
| `packages/mcp-server-revit/pyproject.toml` | `version` |
| `packages/mcp-server-revit/manifest.json` | `version` (MCP bundle) |
| `server.json` | `version`, package `version`, release download URL |
| `packages/revit-bridge-addin/RevitBridge.csproj` | `Version`, `AssemblyVersion`, `FileVersion`, `InformationalVersion` |
| `packages/navisworks-bridge-addin/`, `rhino-bridge-addin/`, `powerbi-bridge-tool/` | `Version` in each `.csproj` |
| `scripts/installer/AECModelBridge.iss` | `AppVersion` |
| `packages/vscode-extension/package.json` | `version` |
| `packages/vscode-extension/package-lock.json` | root version and root package version |

`AssemblyVersion` and `FileVersion` are four-part numbers, so `1.3.0` becomes `1.3.0.0` and any pre-release suffix is dropped there.

`server.json` also carries a `fileSha256` for the `.mcpb` bundle. That hash only exists once the release is built, so the publish workflow refreshes it. Do not edit it by hand.

The release workflow also compiles, tests and packages the VS Code extension.
It passes the versioned `.vsix` to `build-release.ps1 -VSCodePackage`, which
includes it in the release directory and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This attaches a
download to a GitHub release; Marketplace publishing is a separate step.

## Cutting a release

1. Fold the changelog fragments into a release section: `python scripts/changelog.py build --version 1.4.0`. This moves every `changes/*.md` file, and any lines still under `## Unreleased`, into `## 1.4.0 - <today>`.
2. Pick the bump and let the script do the edits:

   ```powershell
   python scripts/version.py bump minor      # or: major | patch
   python scripts/version.py set 1.4.0-rc.1  # or set an exact version
   ```

   This rewrites every file above and keeps the `## 1.4.0` section from step 1 (it renames `## Unreleased` instead when step 1 was skipped).
3. Check, commit, tag and push:

   ```powershell
   python scripts/version.py check
   git commit -am "chore(release): 1.4.0"
   git tag v1.4.0
   git push --follow-tags
   ```

4. The **Build GitHub Release** workflow starts on the tag. It confirms the tag, `VERSION`, every manifest and the changelog agree, runs the Python tests, builds the add-in and installer bundle, and publishes the GitHub release with the changelog section as its notes.
5. For stable tags the release workflow then starts **Publish MCP Server**, which fills in the bundle hash and publishes to the MCP Registry. Pre-releases are not sent to the registry.

If the tag and `VERSION` disagree, or the changelog has no section for that version, the release stops before building anything.

To rebuild an existing release, run **Build GitHub Release** by hand and enter the tag (for example `v1.4.0`). It re-uploads the files and replaces the notes.

## Checks that run automatically

- **Every push and pull request:** CI runs `python scripts/version.py check`. If someone edits one manifest by hand, the build fails and prints what is out of step and the command that fixes it.
- **Every tag:** the release workflow runs the same check with `--tag`, so a mistyped tag cannot ship.

## Command reference

```text
python scripts/version.py show               print the current version
python scripts/version.py check [--tag vX]   fail on drift (and on tag/changelog mismatch)
python scripts/version.py set X.Y.Z          set an exact version, roll the changelog
python scripts/version.py bump minor         increment major, minor or patch
python scripts/version.py notes [X.Y.Z]      print one changelog section (used for release notes)
```

Add `--no-changelog` to `set` or `bump` if you do not want the changelog touched.

## Revit years in a release

Every release ships one package per supported Revit year: `aec-model-bridge-revit-2024-1.3.1.zip` through `aec-model-bridge-revit-2027-1.3.1.zip`. Each zip holds only that year's add-in binaries plus the installer scripts. The `.mcpb` bundle and the Python wheel are shared by all years.

To rebuild a single year by hand, run **Build GitHub Release** and set `revit_version` to that year instead of `All`. For local testing of one year, build it directly:

```powershell
./scripts/build-addin.ps1 -RevitVersion 2026 -Configuration Release
```

# Licensing

AEC Model Bridge version 1.1.0 and later is available under your choice of:

1. the [GNU General Public License version 3 or later](LICENSE), with the
   [AEC Model Bridge Revit Linking Exception](LICENSES/Revit-Linking-Exception.txt);
   or
2. a separate commercial license agreed in writing with the applicable
   copyright holders.

## Why This Model

The GPL option aligns the project with community projects such as pyRevit and
Bonsai. The Revit Linking Exception is a narrow additional permission that
allows the GPL-covered add-in to load and operate through Autodesk's
proprietary Revit APIs without making Autodesk software GPL-covered.

The exception does not permit AEC Model Bridge code to be incorporated into
another proprietary application or proprietary add-in.

## GPL-3.0-or-later Option

The GPL option is free and may be used for any purpose, including commercial
and private internal use. You may inspect, modify, and redistribute the
software subject to GPL-3.0-or-later and the Revit Linking Exception.

The GPL does not require private modifications to be published merely because
they are used inside one organization. When you convey covered software, or a
combined derivative work governed by the GPL, the GPL's license, notice, and
corresponding-source obligations apply. Whether separately communicating
programs form one combined work is fact-specific.

An open-source license cannot, by itself, require every enterprise using the
software internally to buy a commercial license.

## Commercial Option

A separate commercial license may be appropriate when you need rights to
distribute a proprietary combined work without GPL copyleft obligations, or
when you require negotiated support, training, warranties, deployment terms,
or custom development.

For commercial licensing terms, contact
[A. Sam Mohammad](mailto:sammohammadwork@gmail.com). A commercial license can
cover only rights controlled by its licensors; third-party components remain
subject to their respective licenses.

## Historical Releases

Versions 1.0.2 and earlier were released under the MIT License. Existing copies
and grants under those releases remain valid. The historical terms are
preserved in [LICENSES/MIT.txt](LICENSES/MIT.txt).

This document is a practical summary, not legal advice. Have qualified counsel
review the linking exception and commercial terms before relying on them for
material licensing decisions.

=== FILE: .github/SUPPORT.md ===

# Support

AEC Model Bridge is maintained by one person, in their own time. This page says where to ask and what to expect.

## Where to ask

| You want to | Go here |
|---|---|
| Report a bug | [Open a bug report](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) |
| Suggest a feature | [Open a feature request](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml) |
| Ask an installation or usage question | [Open a support question](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/issues/new) and include the details below |
| Report a security problem | Use [private reporting](https://github.com/Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge/security/advisories/new). Read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) first. Do not open a public issue. |
| Report unacceptable behaviour | See [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) |
| Ask about licensing or a commercial licence | Read [LICENSING.md](../LICENSING.md) |
| Ask about the name or logo | Read [TRADEMARKS.md](../docs/legal/TRADEMARKS.md) |
| Fix or improve something yourself | Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) |

Before you open an issue, search the existing ones. Check [docs/install.md](../docs/install.md) and [docs/compatibility.md](../docs/compatibility.md) too.

## What to include

A good report lets someone else repeat the problem. Please give:

- the AEC Model Bridge version (the `VERSION` file, or the installer or release name)
- your Revit year, or say that you used mock mode (`MCP_REVIT_MODE=mock`)
- your Windows version and Python version
- the AI client you used (Claude Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, Codex, or other)
- the steps you took, what you expected and what happened
- the relevant lines from the audit log, `%APPDATA%\AECModelBridge\Logs\bridge.jsonl`

Remove model names, file paths, server names and credentials you do not want public. Never paste secrets.

## What is supported

- Revit 2024 to 2027. See [docs/target-frameworks-and-dependencies.md](../docs/target-frameworks-and-dependencies.md).
- Python 3.11 to 3.13.
- The latest release. See the table in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#supported-versions) and [docs/deprecation-policy.md](../docs/deprecation-policy.md).

## What is not supported

- **Live Revit on anything but Windows.** Revit runs only on Windows, so the add-in does too. On Linux and macOS you can run the server in mock mode and read the code. The Linux CI job is experimental.
- **Clients that have not been tested.** [docs/compatibility.md](../docs/compatibility.md) lists which clients are documented and which are not tested. Reports from other clients are welcome, but fixing them is best effort.
- **Navisworks and Power BI.** The compatibility page marks both as in progress.
- **Revit versions before 2024 or after 2027.**
- **Help with your own Revit models, templates or standards.** Please ask a colleague or a Revit forum for that.
- **Releases that are not the latest**, apart from what [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says.
- **Custom forks and modified builds.**

## What to expect

There is no support contract, no service level and no promised response time. One maintainer reads issues when time allows. That can mean days, and sometimes weeks.

For security reports, [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) states the targets the project aims for. Those are goals for one person, not a guarantee.

Issues that are clear, small and repeatable get looked at first. Reports with no version, no steps or no log may be closed with a request for more detail.

If you need guaranteed help, see the commercial licence option in [LICENSING.md](../LICENSING.md).

=== FILE: docs/issue-guide.md ===

# Issue guide

How issues in this repository are titled, labelled, scheduled and closed. Written for contributors and coding agents that file or rewrite issues.

The forms live in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. The label list, with colours and descriptions, is `.github/labels.yml`.

## Forms

| Form | Use it for | Default labels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bug report | A tool, the add-in, the panel or the installer does not behave as documented. | `type: bug`, `status: triage` |
| Feature request | A task you cannot do today. Problem first, then the proposed behaviour. | `type: feature`, `status: triage` |
| Documentation | A page that is wrong, missing, out of date or unclear. | `type: docs`, `area: docs`, `status: triage` |
| Live Revit verification | Maintainers only. A run sheet for checks that need Windows and a live Revit. | `type: task`, `status: needs-live-verification` |

Security problems never go in a public issue. Use private reporting (see `SECURITY.md`).

## Titles

Format: `<area>: <what is wrong or what is added>`, in sentence case, without a trailing full stop.

- A bug title states the observed fault and the condition: `snapshot: sheet_view_audit reports 0 views because views are not captured`.
- A feature title states the capability in plain words, not the implementation: `qa: check door fire rating against the host wall rating`.
- A task title starts with a verb: `security: route the remaining snapshot_id path joins through safe_child`.
- A tracking issue starts with `Tracking:` and names the outcome: `Tracking: MCP protocol features for 1.7`.
- A live check starts with `verify:` and names the scope and Revit version: `verify: 1.6 release on Revit 2024 and 2026`.
- Use the tool, file or setting name in backticks when it is the subject. Do not put type, priority or version in the title; labels and milestones carry them.
- Avoid one or two word titles such as `IFC diff`. A reader of the issue list should know what changes without opening it.

## Body

Every issue body uses these sections, in this order. Leave a section out only when it has nothing true to say.

1. **Context**: what exists today and who is affected. One short paragraph.
2. **Problem** or **Motivation**: what fails, or what task is blocked. For a bug, quote the error and give steps.
3. **Evidence**: file paths with line numbers, commands and their output, live results with Revit version. Only facts that were observed. Mark anything not observed as UNVERIFIED.
4. **Proposed approach**: the change, the files it touches, and the tests that cover it. If there are two real options, list both with the recommended one first and the reason.
5. **Acceptance criteria**: a checklist (see below).
6. **Out of scope**: what this issue does not do, so reviewers can hold the line.
7. **Related**: links to issues, PRs, ADRs and docs.

Do not write "ask the owner" or "needs a decision" in the body. If the approach is not settled, state the options and the recommendation, and add `status: needs-design`. The discussion happens in the comments; the outcome goes into the body or an ADR.

## Acceptance criteria

- Write them as a Markdown checklist, one observable result per line.
- Each line can be checked by a named test, a command, or a single live run. "Works well" is not a criterion; "returns `complete=true` on the canonical fixture" is.
- State the negative case where it matters: what must still be refused, what old files must still load.
- Every behaviour change carries two standing criteria from `AGENTS.md`: a test, and one fragment file `changes/<issue-or-branch>.md`. A change to tools also regenerates `docs/tools-generated.md`.
- Every change that touches model writes carries: no write path skips `plan_actions`, human approval and `execute_plan`.
- If a criterion needs a live Revit, say so on that line. Code can merge with that line open; the issue then gets `status: needs-live-verification` and stays open until the check is recorded.

## Labels

Each issue has exactly one `type:` label, one or more `area:` labels and, once accepted, one `priority:` label. `size:` is optional. `status:` labels say what the issue waits on and are removed when the wait ends.

| Group | Labels | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type:` | `bug`, `feature`, `docs`, `task`, `tech-debt`, `tracking` | Kind of work. `task` covers review, verification and maintenance. `tracking` groups other issues. |
| `area:` | `approval`, `security`, `server`, `mcp`, `addin`, `panel`, `snapshot`, `qa`, `interop`, `modules`, `install`, `ci`, `docs` | Part of the system. All areas share one colour so they read as a group. |
| `priority:` | `P0`, `P1`, `P2`, `P3` | P0: a wrong result shown as correct, a security exposure or data loss. P1: blocks the milestone. P2: planned. P3: not planned. |
| `size:` | `S`, `M`, `L` | About a day, a few days, a week or more. `L` usually needs a design note first. |
| `status:` | `triage`, `needs-info`, `needs-repro`, `needs-design`, `blocked`, `in-progress`, `needs-live-verification`, `verified-live`, `maintainer-only` | What the issue waits on. `maintainer-only` marks work that needs repo admin access or the maintainer's licensed Revit; outside contributors should pick other issues. |
| contributor | `good first issue`, `help wanted` | See below. |
| `resolution:` | `duplicate`, `wontfix`, `invalid`, `as-designed` | Why an issue closed without a change. Add a comment with the reason. |
| `pr:` | `needs-review`, `ready-to-merge`, `conflicts`, `tests`, `refactor` | Pull requests only. |

Dependabot applies `dependencies`, `python`, `python:uv`, `.NET`, `github_actions` and `javascript` to its pull requests. Do not use them on issues.

## Good first issue

Apply `good first issue` only when all of these hold:

- It can be built and tested in mock mode on Linux, without Windows or Revit.
- The body names the files to change and the test file to extend.
- It touches one module or one doc, and does not change the approval gate.
- The acceptance criteria are complete; a newcomer does not need to make a design choice.

`help wanted` means the issue is accepted and open to outside contributors. Contributors comment on the issue before starting; see `CONTRIBUTING.md` for the licensing note on code contributions.

## Milestones

- A version milestone (for example `1.6`) holds the issues that must close, or be explicitly moved, before that release.
- `Backlog` holds accepted issues with no release planned.
- An issue without a milestone has not been triaged.
- At release time, open issues in the version milestone are either finished, moved with a comment, or block the release.

## Tracking issues

Open a tracking issue (`type: tracking`) when:

- a goal needs three or more issues, or spans the server, the add-in and the panel, or
- a release needs a set of live checks across several features.

A tracking issue states the goal, lists the child issues as a task list (`- [ ] #123`), and gives the exit criteria for the whole group. Child issues stay small and self-contained; the tracking issue holds no implementation detail. Close it when every item is done or moved out with a comment.

## Live verification

Behaviour that depends on Revit cannot be proven in CI. When code merges with a live check outstanding:

1. Keep the issue open with `status: needs-live-verification`, or list the check in the release's live verification issue.
2. Record the result with Revit version, model type and commit.
3. On PASS, replace the label with `status: verified-live` and remove UNVERIFIED from the affected docs. On FAIL, open a bug and link it.

`docs/release-checklist.md` section 2 lists the standing live checks.

## Closing

- Close through a pull request with `Fixes #N` in the description or commit.
- When closing without a change, add one `resolution:` label and a comment with the reason.
- `status: needs-info` issues close after 14 days without the requested information. They can be reopened when it arrives.
